item.title: Climate crisis deepens risks for children, especially adolescent girls
item.description:
Children are bearing the brunt of climate change, with extreme heat, frequent floods, disease and displacement threatening their health, nutrition and education.
Adolescent girls face additional risks, particularly in maintaining menstrual hygiene and accessing safe sanitation during disasters.
According to UNICEF’s “Children’s Climate Risk Report 2026”, published on June 16, nearly 59 million children in Bangladesh — almost the entire child population — face at least one climate-related hazard.
Around 53 million, or 89.5%, are exposed to at least three such risks simultaneously.
The report estimates that 98.44% of children are at risk of drought, 91.23% of tropical storms and 54.18% of river flooding. Agricultural and weather-related droughts threaten 91.83% and 90.26% of children respectively.
The effects extend beyond disasters, disrupting access to safe drinking water, sanitation, healthcare and education, particularly in coastal and flood-prone areas.
A Save the Children survey found that 80% of participating children became ill following disasters or heatwaves, while 53% struggled to access safe drinking water. Weather-related disruptions kept 49% of school-going children out of school during the past year.
Conducted from October 9 to 17, the survey involved 1,375 children aged 10-17 from climate-vulnerable areas in 38 districts. A total of 172 child researchers from the National Children's Task Force (NCTF) conducted the interviews.
Around 96% of respondents had experienced at least one disaster in the previous two years, including heatwaves (55%) and floods (42%).
“Children in Bangladesh are in no way responsible for creating this crisis, yet they are suffering the most,” said Save the Children in Bangladesh Country Director Shumon Sengupta, stressing the need to address their specific concerns.
The challenges are particularly acute for adolescent girls in coastal areas.
Jayanti Sarker, 16, from Deluti Union in Khulna's Paikgachha Upazila, said floods and cyclones have repeatedly inundated her home. During severe disasters, her family has to take shelter in cyclone centres or other people's homes.
“Staying in shelters is particularly difficult for girls like us. During menstruation, we already feel physically uncomfortable. On top of that, hundreds of people have to share the same toilets and bathrooms. Some develop infections,” she said.
Jayanti, a student at Paikgachha Government College, said prolonged stays in shelters disrupt education, while floodwaters often destroy household belongings and school materials. Her younger brother has also become reluctant to study after returning from shelters.
Another local teenager, 15-year-old Antara Sarker, said her family had once spent nearly a month in a cyclone shelter. Floodwaters submerged her books and other belongings, leaving her unable to continue her studies.
She added that saline water and inadequate sanitation during disasters increase health risks for girls, while access to personal hygiene facilities and healthcare remains limited.
Public health expert Mushtaq Hossain warned that floods and droughts could disrupt food production, leading to nutritional shortages, malnutrition and weakened immunity among children. He stressed the need for safe water, nutritious food and timely medical care.
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare MA Muhit has stressed the importance of delivering health information to schools during heatwaves.
He suggested deploying mobile health teams or arranging visits by nurses and doctors, even where schools do not have permanent medical staff. He also called for better early-warning systems, timely disaster preparedness and research into health risks in flood-affected areas.
Experts say long-term planning must prioritise children's health, nutrition and education, with safe drinking water, hygienic toilets and essential healthcare ensured at schools and shelters. Disaster management plans must also address the specific needs of adolescent girls.

item.title: Bangladesh loses garment orders as India gains ground
item.description:
Global fashion giants such as Zara and H&M have shifted nearly 10% of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian countries in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs chipped away at the country's competitive edge in the global garment market.
Reuters reported the development, citing three Bangladeshi garment factory owners. The owners said international brands had shifted orders worth around $254 million from Bangladesh between November 1 and 18, with most of them going to neighbouring India.
The shift poses a major threat to one of Bangladesh's key economic sectors, with industry insiders warning that the impact could persist long after the current unrest subsides.
Industry leaders said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty had weakened Bangladesh's traditional advantage of low-cost garment production. As a result, global brands are increasingly turning to alternative sourcing destinations, despite Bangladesh being the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.
According to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), ongoing protests have already caused production losses worth more than $400 million. The garment sector accounts for more than 80% of the country's total export earnings and around 40% of manufacturing employment.
India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversion, while buyers are also turning to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply chain risks and ensure timely deliveries.
Following the Reuters report, shares of Indian textile companies surged on Friday. Gokaldas Exports gained as much as 11%, while Trident rose 5%.
Pressure on the industry intensified after the government approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers on Wednesday. The increase, the smallest in four decades, fell far short of workers' demands for more than double their existing wages, triggering fresh clashes with police.
Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, described the wage increase as "satisfactory" and expressed hope that all workers would return to work from Saturday. Factory owners, however, said the increase would further narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India.
Speaking on condition of anonymity, three factory owners said brands such as Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer and Celio were shifting orders elsewhere amid the unrest, with India receiving most of the diverted business.
Inditex, Zara's parent company, declined to comment, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
BGMEA Director Md M Mohiuddin Chowdhury said the wage increase had pushed up production costs at a time when buyers were demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries was intensifying.
BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan, however, said that temporarily shifting some orders elsewhere could help minimise financial losses while retaining international buyers. He did not name any specific brands.
Factory owners are particularly concerned that orders shifted to other countries may never return if buyers reassess their sourcing strategies and establish new supplier relationships.
The energy crisis, exacerbated by tensions in the Middle East, has also disrupted production and forced factories to rely on more expensive alternative energy sources.
Chowdhury said buyers were now prioritising timely delivery over price. Indian suppliers can deliver garments nearly a week faster than their Bangladeshi counterparts, while suppliers in Vietnam and Cambodia can complete deliveries up to 15 days sooner.
Competitors can complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with around 120 days in Bangladesh, he said.
Factories around Dhaka have suffered an estimated 20 to 25 days of production disruption due to the unrest. Many are considering overtime work and costly air freight to meet shipment deadlines.
Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which supplies garments to European brands, said most of his buyers had stopped placing new orders since November 1 because of the unrest.
"They are telling us that our orders have been diverted elsewhere, suspended or cancelled," he said.
Political tensions surrounding the possible return of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to Dhaka from India have also heightened fears of renewed instability.
Industry leaders have warned that unless stability is restored, the temporary diversion of orders could become permanent, with buyers unlikely to return to Bangladesh even after the situation normalises.

item.title: RMG wage crisis: Who pays for growth, and who pays the price?
item.description:
The readymade garments’ (RMG) industry in Bangladesh is once again confronting a serious labour crisis. Workers were protesting on the streets in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia, Narayanganj, and Dhaka for the minimum wage of Tk 30,000 per month, which is currently Tk 12,500. In early November, when unrest was at its peak, the BGMEA said that 529 factories had suspended production, putting nearly a million workers out of work.
The government acted swiftly. The six-member wage board was established on November 1 and both sides have agreed to the effectivity of the new wage board from December 1 with a revised wage to take effect in January.
Workers have a case The minimum wage was last hiked in late 2023 from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500. Much of this increase has since been lost amid three years of high inflation. The inflation rate was 8.27% in October 2026. Food prices have slowed, but non-food inflation is increasing to 9.89% , its highest level in 41 months, and a worker's budget is being dominated by rent, transport, healthcare, and schooling costs. According to official data, inflation is now running at a higher rate than wages for 57 months in a row. The Clean Clothes Campaign (CCC) (in May and August, 2026) survey of 1,094 garment workers, carried out from May to August, revealed that 89% were unable to pay their basic expenses for their families; 70% of the workers took loans from friends or relatives, and 28% took the loans from additional overtime. These early results are in line with what reporters are hearing on the ground. Workers are being forced to take difficult decisions like meals eliminated, medical care deferred, and children removed from school.
However, the jobs argument is a two-way paradigm. The cost of labour is about 10-13% of industry costs. International experience, as in Germany with a minimum wage, indicates that job loss is not inevitable, but instead varies with the extent and speed of the wage increase and the capacity of firms to respond. Unrest also leads to factory closures, cancelled shipments, and job losses, and buyers are aware that a marginally cheaper supplier is an expensive supplier if their production is continually disrupted.
The missing party at the table
The global buyer is the most under-heard player in this debate. Brands are driving ever higher standards for safety, environment, traceability, and carbon reporting, and are tough to bargain with regarding price.
A previous ILO survey revealed that there is little evidence that buyers were willing to pass on minimum wage increases to Bangladeshi suppliers. A wage increase that the buyer will not partake in is pushed back onto the factories and, ultimately, onto the owners and workers.
Responsible sourcing and practices that squeeze suppliers cannot coexist. When brands promote decent work, they should make this commitment publicly and in their contracts to pay for the labour-cost share of the new wage, whether through ring-fenced wage components in the order prices, or with longer term sourcing commitments. There should be a coordinated push by the BGMEA, BKMEA, and the government, not only by the factories.
A national problem
The RMG sector currently supports about four million jobs, the majority of which are held by women, and generates over 80% of the income from merchandise exports. The delay of shipments in the peak season also affects factory cash flows and foreign-exchange receipts; it also reduces the spending of workers’ households.
The unrest has also caused anxiety among buyers as Bangladesh is preparing for its graduation from the LDC category and the end of trade preferences. The economy can ill afford another self-inflicted blow as private-sector credit growth is around 4%.
There are four steps that would help to break the cycle.
First of all , the wage board’s decision must be based upon transparent evidence: Household expenditure, inflation, productivity, and industry capacity. They must also state their reasoning for the decision. The schedule must be short, front-loaded, binding, and not be postponed.
Secondly , the new labour law stipulates that annual changes should only occur between full revisions in every three years; this should be adjusted to inflation.
Third , small factories should be put on alert. Identify sources of working capital, a stable supply of energy, a stable source of productivity training, and a commitment to full implementation of the new wage.
Fourth , industrial relations need to be formalized in the institutional structure of independent trade unions, working participation committees, and effective grievance procedures, and blacklisting and retaliation against workers who protest must stop.
The choice Bangladesh cannot postpone
Bangladesh is the second biggest apparel exporter in the world. Yet, much of this has been due to its low labour cost - an advantage that is fading and one that’s never been a strong base. Its future competitiveness must be based on productivity, skills, technology, and higher value products, rather than retaining low-paid employees.
A garment industry that exports prosperity to the world but cannot adequately sustain the livelihoods of its own workers is not a model of sustainable development. Bangladesh must now decide whether it wants to remain a low-wage manufacturing destination or become a globally competitive economy built on productive, skilled and fairly compensated workers.
Dr Md Sohel Rana is an Associate Professor, IUBAT Business School.

item.title: Govt steps up security after attacks on 104 Grameen Bank offices
item.description:
The government has stepped up security measures and law enforcement operations following a wave of attacks on Grameen Bank branches and offices, with police instructed to strengthen patrols, monitor vulnerable establishments and bring those responsible to justice.
However, the measures have yet to stop the attacks, which damaged 104 branches and offices across the country between November 10 and 25, according to Bangladesh Bank. Operations at 29 branches remain suspended over security concerns.
Police Headquarters data show that, up to November 23, 34 incidents involving Grameen Bank had led to eight cases and 19 general diaries (GDs), with eight people arrested.
Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman disclosed the figures at a press conference on November 24.
Police Headquarters Spokesperson AIG (Media) Kamarum Munira said that relevant police units had been instructed to identify those involved and bring them to justice.
Local police have also been directed to take precautionary measures, increase surveillance at vulnerable branches and offices, and strengthen patrols according to the security situation, she said.
Requests for additional security from Bangladesh Bank and Grameen Bank authorities were also being considered, she added, assuring that police were taking the matter seriously.
Amid the continuing attacks, Grameen Bank Managing Director Sarder Akhter Hamed has sought the home minister's intervention.
In a letter, he called for impartial investigations, swift identification and prosecution of those responsible, and security for the bank's branches, offices, assets, employees and members across the country.
The bank also urged better coordination among government agencies and law enforcement bodies to ensure effective protection.
Despite the ongoing police operations, the number of affected branches increased from 72 in 40 districts by November 19 to 97 by November 23, eventually reaching 104 by November 25.
The attacks have damaged buildings, furniture, documents and other assets, while leaving employees and borrowers concerned about their safety.
Alongside law enforcement measures, Bangladesh Bank is examining whether individuals or groups provided financial backing for the attacks.
Central bank Spokesperson Arief Hossain Khan said on Thursday that the bank was investigating possible financing and working to prevent suspicious financial transactions.
No details have yet been disclosed about suspected financiers, identified transactions or any bank accounts frozen in connection with the incidents.
The central bank has also warned that the disruption could have wider consequences for rural communities.
With Boro-season lending underway, the closure of 29 branches has left borrowers in affected areas struggling to access agricultural financing. Livestock farmers preparing for Eid-ul-Azha may also face difficulties securing loans.
Grameen Bank operates across all 64 districts, with 261 area offices, 40 zonal offices and 40 zonal audit offices. Borrowers own 90% of its shares, while the government holds the remaining 10%.
Grameen Bank founder and Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus has called for an end to the attacks and swift prosecution of those responsible.
In a statement on November 23, he described the incidents as apparently organised and alleged that “Joy Bangla” slogans were chanted during some attacks.
He said 97% of the bank's borrowers were women and warned that the attacks were undermining efforts to improve their economic conditions and dignity.
He also thanked law enforcement agencies for taking prompt action in some cases and urged the international community to speak out against the attacks.
The United Nations has called for a full investigation by Bangladeshi authorities, while the United States has urged restraint and expressed support for peaceful expression under Bangladeshi law.

item.title: Tahsif death mystery remains unsolved despite 40 statements
item.description:
Investigators have recorded statements from at least 40 people and examined evidence to establish what happened before and after former Bangladesh Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri’s death. However, they are yet to determine whether he was murdered, died by suicide or was killed in an accident.
More than a month after his body was recovered from the Turag River, Naval Police are still awaiting the full autopsy report, which they say will be crucial in determining the cause of death.
Investigators are also examining circumstantial evidence and information gathered from various sources rather than relying solely on medical findings.
According to police, Tahsif left his residence in the RAJUK Apartment Project in Uttara’s Sector 18 on October 27 on a motorcycle belonging to Ahmed Shahriar Dip. He later went to a bar in Sector 13 with a young woman he knew. Dip was also present there.
The following afternoon, on October 28, Naval Police received a call through the national emergency service 999 reporting a body floating in the Turag River near Rajbari Ghat in Uttarkhan. His identity was established through an iPhone found in his trouser pocket. He was 28.
The inquest report described the body as approximately 5ft 7in tall, with black hair and a short beard and moustache. His eyes and mouth were closed, and blood was seen coming from his nose. Both hands were bent towards his head, with the fists clenched, while his abdomen was swollen.
The report found no visible abnormalities in the chest, abdomen, back, legs or genital area. No external injury marks were recorded. He was wearing a black full-sleeved kabli shirt and white trousers.
However, the absence of visible injuries does not establish the cause of death.
Assistant Professor of Forensic Medicine at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College, Nashat Jabin, said samples from Tahsif’s stomach, liver, kidneys and blood had been sent for laboratory tests.
The full autopsy report will be prepared after the test results are received, she said, adding that the cause of death could then be determined.
Naval Police Chief and Additional Inspector General Rezaul Karim said investigators were considering murder, suicide and accidental death.
At least 40 people have been questioned, and information gathered during the investigation is being cross-checked, he said.
The autopsy findings will be assessed alongside other evidence before investigators reach a conclusion and submit their report to the court.
Meanwhile, two people — Ahmed Shahriar Dip, a close acquaintance of Tahsif, and a young woman he knew — have been arrested in the murder case filed by his father, AKM Enayetul Karim. Both are currently in jail.

item.title: UK police arrest 6 over clash involving NCP, Awami League activists
item.description:
London's Metropolitan Police have arrested 6 people over a clash involving National Citizen Party (NCP) and Awami League leaders and activists in East London, following a reception ceremony for NCP Convener Nahid Islam.
The arrests were made between November 24 and 26. All 6 have been released on bail while further investigations continue. However, police have not confirmed the names or political identities of those arrested.
According to a report by Prothom Alo, Nancy Bauhurst, media and public relations manager of the London Metropolitan Police, provided the information in response to an email from the newspaper.
The incident took place on November 16 following a reception ceremony for Nahid Islam at the May Fair Venue on High Road in the Chadwell Heath area of East London.
A chase and counter-chase broke out between NCP leaders and activists and Awami League leaders and activists. At one point, Awami League activists and supporters allegedly beat NCP leaders and activists with tree branches.
The Metropolitan Police said they received reports of disorder on High Road at 9:59pm on the night of the incident, involving around 50 men. Some became involved in violence, threw various objects and caused property damage.
Police officers arrived at the scene, but those involved had dispersed by then. Three people injured in the incident were taken to hospital by the London Ambulance Service. Their injuries were not serious.
Police said they conducted investigative activities, including an extensive review of CCTV footage, to identify those involved in the clash.
As part of the investigation, 6 people aged 23, 24, 25, 31, 38 and 49 were arrested between Tuesday and Thursday last week.
They were arrested on suspicion of involvement in violent disorder under Section 2 of the United Kingdom's Public Order Act 1986. However, police did not provide any information on whether formal charges would be brought against them.
Detective Chief Inspector Steve Mulkahy of the London Metropolitan Police, who is leading the investigation, said: “This violent disorder has caused deep concern among local residents of Redbridge. Many were afraid to leave their homes. When police arrived at the scene quickly, those involved in the disorder left the area. My team is working tirelessly to identify those involved in the incident.”
The Metropolitan Police did not disclose the names or political identities of those arrested when asked about the matter.
The Metropolitan Police said the investigation into the clash is ongoing. They have urged anyone with CCTV or vehicle dashboard camera footage that could assist the investigation to contact 101 and quote reference number CAD 7004/16NOV.

item.title: Government plans Tk14,000 crore agriculture transformation project
item.description:
The government is planning to undertake a Tk14,000 crore project to transform the country's agriculture sector from production-based farming into an entrepreneurship- and market-oriented system.
In Bangladesh, the broader agriculture sector, covering crops, livestock, fisheries and forestry, accounts for roughly 11%-11.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) and employs around 45% of the workforce, while supporting food security and rural livelihoods.
The project aims to bring agriculture, livestock and fisheries under a common framework to develop productive partnerships, digitize agricultural services and ensure food security, according to sources close to the project.
The preliminary plan for the Bangladesh Agri Entrepreneurship Project (BAP) is being prepared with proposed financing of $100 million from the World Bank.
Its main objective is to strengthen production and marketing systems by establishing effective linkages among farmers, agri-based entrepreneurs and relevant stakeholders.
Under the proposed project, plans include strengthening partnerships between farmers and agri-based entrepreneurs, developing digital infrastructure for public services and ensuring traceability of agricultural products from production to marketing.
The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Department of Livestock Services and Department of Fisheries will be involved in implementing the project, with the DAE being considered as the lead implementing agency.
Project lead focal point Shakhawat Hossain Sharif said the financing, expenditure heads and activities of the project had not yet been finalized.
The project size and action plan may change following discussions and agreements between the World Bank and the government. A technical note on the project is currently being prepared, he said.
The Agriculture Ministry said the proposed initiative is a continuation of the Program on Agricultural and Rural Transformation for Nutrition (PARTNER), launched in July 2023 with World Bank support.
Building on the experience of the existing program, the new project aims to make agriculture more productive, market-oriented and climate-resilient.
Project lead Shakhawat Hossain Sharif said four major components were being proposed under the project. These would be determined based on field-level needs, government priorities and commitments outlined in the election manifesto.
A preparation team has also been formed for this purpose, he said.
Under the first component, titled Productive Partnerships, $225 million is proposed to develop productive partnerships.
The main objective is to strengthen production and marketing systems through effective linkages among farmers, agri-based entrepreneurs and relevant stakeholders.
The second component aims to develop digital public infrastructure to make government support in agriculture more effective.
A proposed $75 million will be allocated to this component to increase the use of digital technology in agricultural services and support systems.
The third component focuses on strengthening food safety and traceability systems from production to market.
A proposed $30 million will be spent on ensuring food safety and improving access to information about the origin and supply chains of agricultural products.
The fourth component includes project management, learning from experience and strengthening coordination among relevant agencies, with a proposed allocation of $20 million.
The total proposed expenditure for the four components is $350 million.
An additional $300 million is planned for the second phase and $250 million for the third phase of the proposed project.
Relevant stakeholders said the emphasis on productive partnerships under the proposed BAP project would create opportunities for coordinated initiatives between farmers and entrepreneurs.

item.title: Zubaida Rahman: Mid-day meals for 1.1cr primary students from 2027
item.description:
Dr Zubaida Rahman, wife of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, on Friday said around 1.1 crore children across the country will receive mid-day meals at all government primary schools from 2027 as part of the government's initiative to ensure child nutrition.
She said the school feeding programme would play an important role in addressing nutritional deficiencies among children, increasing school attendance and ensuring continuity of their formal education.
"At present, around 3.1 million students in 151 of the country's 500 upazilas receive nutritious meals every day. From 2027, the programme will be expanded to all government primary schools across the 500 upazilas, benefiting 11 million children," she said.
Dr Zubaida Rahman, also Vice-President of Ziaur Rahman Foundation, was speaking at the prize-giving ceremony of a cooking competition held as part of National Livestock Week at the old trade fair ground beside Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University in Agargaon.
She stressed monitoring of food quality by involving mothers, and proposed district- and upazila-level cooking competitions to make school meals tastier, more nutritious and more accessible.
The physician said hygienic cooking, locally available vegetables, protein-rich foods and dairy products, along with mothers' involvement, could improve children's nutrition.
Citing UN statistics, she said 25.1% of children under five in Bangladesh suffer from stunting. "To achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his government have taken various initiatives," she said.
Five participants were awarded from 300 entries. Tahera Islam Tinni of Madaripur won first place, Abu Abdullah Md Siam second and Sajia Ferdous of Rangpur third. The winners received crests, certificates and cheques.
Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid presided over the programme. State Minister Sultan Salauddin Tuku, Secretary Md Delwar Hossain and Director General (in-charge) of the Department of Livestock Services, Agriculturist Md Shahjaman Khan, among others, were present.

item.title: Passengers suffer as Benapole-Dhaka train services suspended for nine days
item.description:
Train services on the Benapole-Dhaka route have remained suspended for nine consecutive days due to security concerns, leaving thousands of passengers across Benapole and several southwestern districts in distress.
The suspension of the Ruposi Bangla Express since November 19 has forced passengers to rely on road transport, resulting in higher travel costs and longer journeys.
A visit to Benapole Railway Station found the premises deserted and unusually quiet in the absence of train services. Students, commuters, and businesspeople who regularly use the route have been among the worst affected. Passengers travelling to Dhaka for urgent purposes are now forced to take buses.
According to railway sources, the authorities have temporarily suspended the Ruposi Bangla Express. Although the train was scheduled to resume operations on Thursday, the railway authorities issued a fresh notice extending the suspension.
Benapole Railway Station Assistant Stationmaster Parvina Khatun said the notice cited the absence of specific information or feedback from the local administration in Gopalganj and adjoining areas regarding the safe operation of trains.
"In the interest of overall railway security, with approval from Railway Bhaban in Dhaka, the operations of the Ruposi Bangla Express on the Dhaka-Benapole-Dhaka route and the Jahanabad Express on the Khulna-Dhaka-Khulna route have been cancelled for Thursday," she said, quoting the notice.
Jessore Railway Station Stationmaster Saiduzzaman said both the Ruposi Bangla Express on the Benapole-Jessore-Dhaka route and the Jahanabad Express on the Khulna-Dhaka route had been temporarily suspended. However, the Jahanabad Express would operate on an alternative route, he confirmed.
The Jahanabad Express will run between Khulna and Dhaka via Poradah and Rajbari. The train will leave Dhaka at 4:10 pm and reach Khulna at 11:35 pm. In the opposite direction, it will depart Khulna at 8:00 am and arrive in Dhaka at 3:10 pm.
The alternative service will stop at Daulatpur, Noapara, Jessore, Mobarakganj, Kotchandpur and Darshana in both directions. It will also make halts at Chuadanga, Alamdanga, Poradah, Kushtia Court, Kamarkhali, Pangsha, Rajbari, Faridpur and Bhanga.
Benapole Railway Station Stationmaster Ainal Haque said the Ruposi Bangla Express service had remained suspended since November 19. He added that arrangements were in place to refund passengers for tickets purchased for the cancelled journeys, he added.

item.title: Khulna pharmacy owner’s son shot following extortion threats
item.description:
Thirteen days after reopening under police protection following extortion threats, a pharmacy in Khulna’s Tutpara was targeted in a shooting on Friday evening, leaving the owner's son injured.
Miscreants arriving on a motorcycle opened fire at Chayanika Pharmacy before fleeing. The victim, Zarifuzzaman Zarif, was shot in the right thigh and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital for treatment.
The pharmacy was under police protection on Friday, as on previous days. However, no police personnel were reportedly present at the premises when the shooting took place.
The pharmacy had remained closed from the night of October 28 to November 14 due to threats over extortion demands, which had created fear and panic. Amid the situation, the Chemists and Druggists Association gave the administration a 3-day ultimatum to bring the situation under control.
Following assurances from police, the pharmacy reopened under police protection on the night of November 14.
Rickshaw driver Wasik Hossain, an eyewitness, said the shooting took place at around 6:30pm on Friday.
He said a person wearing a burqa came in front of the pharmacy when no police personnel were present. A motorcycle then arrived and stopped nearby.
The burqa-clad person suddenly pulled out a firearm and fired a shot inside the pharmacy, triggering shouting and commotion, Wasik said.
He added that a bloodied person was later brought out of the pharmacy. As the area became deserted following the gunfire, he took his rickshaw forward and transported the injured man to a nearby clinic.
Khulna Sadar police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Lokman Hossain said miscreants arrived on a motorcycle in front of the pharmacy in the evening, opened fire and fled.
He said the bullet struck the right thigh of Zarifuzzaman Zarif, son of pharmacy owner A B M Doulatuzzaman. The injured man was admitted to Khulna Medical College Hospital.
The OC said police regularly provide security at the pharmacy, adding that the personnel may have been at some distance from the premises when the shooting occurred.

item.title: Fire at Inani gas well brought under control after a month
item.description:
The fire at a gas well in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has been brought under control after nearly a month of continuous efforts by the Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (Bapex), paving the way for further technical operations and exploration.
On Friday morning, Bapex installed a 30-inch casing using a specialised technical procedure, extinguishing the flames that had been burning at different points on the surface.
Bapex officials described the operation as highly hazardous. They said the gas flow was diverted through a line connected to the casing, reducing pressure at the wellhead and allowing the fire to die out.
With the blaze contained, the next phase of work is underway. According to Bapex's plan, drill pipes will be reinserted to reach a depth of around 1,000 feet. Specialised drilling mud will be used during the process to control and stabilise pressure inside the well.
Officials said the operation would help balance formation pressure and seal the pathway through which gas had been escaping. Further steps will be taken to ensure the well is completely secure.
Shyamal Kumar Balu, a department head at Bapex, said the fire was extinguished by installing the casing and controlling the gas flow through a diversion line.
He said the well would now be secured in stages and prepared for future exploration.
Once the well is made safe, Bapex plans to conduct further geological and seismic surveys in the area. The findings will be analysed to assess whether commercially viable gas reserves are present and determine the scope for future exploration and extraction.
After bringing the fire under control, Bapex technical officials collected two samples of gas escaping through the pipeline.
Bapex Manager SM Nafisul Arfan said the samples would be sent to Dhaka for testing. The analysis is expected to provide information about the gas's chemical composition, quality and potential commercial value, helping guide future exploration plans.
Bapex official Rakibul Hasan also confirmed that two samples had been collected and would be sent to Dhaka for analysis.
The fire's containment has brought relief to local residents, who had been concerned about the heat, smoke and safety risks during the month-long incident. Bapex officials, however, said several critical tasks remained, including securing the well, managing underground pressure and assessing the gas.
A team of experts will continue working at the site over the next few days.
On October 27, gas began erupting from underground with considerable pressure while a deep tube well was being installed near the Choto Bridge area in Inani union of Cox's Bazar.
Shortly afterwards, a spark from a nearby electrical line ignited the gas, setting the area ablaze. The fire continued burning day and night for nearly a month.
A team of Bapex experts arrived at the site soon after the incident and began containment efforts. The operation involved reducing gas pressure, establishing a safety perimeter, deploying specialised equipment and conducting technical assessments.
The fire was finally brought under control on Friday following the installation of the casing.

item.title: 109 platoons of BGB deployed in Dhaka, five other districts
Eight Bangladeshis return home after two years in Indian jails
Bangladesh to join Franco-Mexican initiative
item.description:
Bangladesh would join the Franco-Mexican initiative to regulate the use of the veto at the Security Council in cases of mass atrocities, said President of the United Nations General Assembly and Foreign Minister of Bangladesh Dr Khalilur Rahman.
He made this commitment at a meeting with French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot in Paris, France on Thursday, according to a statement of the French Foreign Ministry.
During the meeting, they talked about the ongoing work at the United Nations General Assembly to promote effective multilateralism and the resolution of conflicts and crises.
Dr Khalilur Rahman pledged that his country would join the Franco-Mexican initiative to regulate the use of the veto at the Security Council in cases of mass atrocities.
The two ministers also discussed how to coordinate their action within the General Assembly to make further progress on this initiative.
The two ministers signalled their commitment to fighting against impunity following the decision by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on the Rohingyas’ situation.
The two ministers also expressed their desire to strengthen bilateral relations as regards the economy, culture, academic cooperation and sustainable development.

Commerce minister: Ramadan prices expected to remain stable
item.description:
Commerce and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir has expressed optimism that prices of essential commodities will remain stable during the upcoming Ramadan, citing adequate supplies in the market.
He made the remarks while responding to journalists after a meeting at the Sylhet District Council auditorium on Friday evening.
Explaining the recent increase in edible oil prices, the minister said costs had risen in the international market and at the sources of imports, prompting an adjustment in domestic prices.
“Bangladesh does not produce soybean or palm oil. When prices rise in the international market, the impact is felt at home, just as local prices fall when global prices decline,” he said.
Under the existing pricing formula, soybean oil should cost slightly more, but the government persuaded importers to maintain the current rate, even applying some pressure, he added.
The minister said the per-litre price is calculated based on the cost and freight (CFR) price in the international market, port charges, processing costs and wastage. Journalists can obtain the pricing formula from the Ministry of Commerce and verify the calculations themselves, he said.

item.title: Workers welcome Tk17,000 minimum wage with rally in Gazipur
item.description:
Garment workers and leaders of several labour organisations held a rally in Gazipur on Friday, congratulating the prime minister, labour minister and wage board for setting the minimum monthly wage for garment workers at Tk17,000.
Organised by the Bangladesh Garment Workers Trade Union Federation, the procession began at Board Bazar around 4:30pm, passed through Signboard Bazar and returned to its starting point.
At a brief gathering after the procession, federation General Secretary Akash Ahmed Babul, Gazipur district committee General Secretary Rasel Mondal, Organising Secretary Mohammad Mazharul Islam and other labour leaders addressed the participants.
The speakers alleged that a vested group was trying to mislead workers and create unrest in industrial areas. They said vandalism, road blockades and other disruptive activities at some factories were putting the livelihoods of workers at risk and threatening the industry.
They called for those involved in vandalism and disorder to be identified and brought to justice, urging workers to resume normal production across Gazipur.
The leaders also called for cooperation between workers and factory owners to keep production running and ensure the continued growth of the garment sector.

item.title: 100 crude bomb blasts, 92 vehicles torched nationwide in 19 days
item.description:
At least 100 crude bomb explosions and arson attacks on 92 vehicles were reported across the country in the past 19 days. During the same period, four police establishments were targeted in arson and vandalism attacks.
In addition, 28 vehicles were set on fire or vandalised, while crude bombs were detonated at three establishments and one vehicle was damaged in an explosion.
Police have so far filed 46 cases and arrested 80 people in connection with the incidents.
According to police sources, the incidents took place in different parts of the country between November 7 and 25. During this period, various types of vehicles were targeted in arson attacks, while police establishments and vehicles also came under attack. The incidents involved arson, vandalism and the use of explosives.
Police data show that 100 crude bomb explosions occurred at different locations across the country during the 19-day period. Arson attacks were reported on 92 vehicles, while four police establishments were targeted with arson and vandalism. Another 28 vehicles were subjected to similar attacks. Crude bomb explosions were also reported at three establishments, with one vehicle damaged in a blast.
Police have launched investigations and operations in different areas to identify and arrest those involved. So far, 46 cases have been filed and 80 people arrested.
Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (Media and Public Relations) at Police Headquarters, said police were on high alert to prevent sabotage and anti-state activities.
"Efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved in the acts of sabotage," she said.
She said police had drawn up a coordinated security plan to maintain law and order. The measures include collecting advance intelligence, increasing surveillance at key locations, intensifying patrols, setting up checkpoints where necessary and ensuring a swift response to any emerging situation.
Special surveillance has also been introduced in vulnerable areas and around important installations, she added.
Munira said police were maintaining heightened vigilance to prevent activities-banned organisations and political parties whose activities have been prohibited from engaging in sabotage, violence or activities that could threaten public security.
Police would take firm action against any attempt to create disorder or undermine law and order, she said, adding that legal measures were being taken to prevent damage to life and property, arson, vandalism and attempts to spread panic.
She said police were working in coordination with other law enforcement agencies, regularly exchanging intelligence and monitoring the situation to strengthen security where necessary.
Ensuring security at public gatherings and important locations, particularly during festive events, while keeping traffic movement normal, has also been prioritised under the plan.
The overall objective is to ensure public safety, maintain law and order and protect people's lives and property, Munira said, adding that police would remain vigilant and resolute in preventing sabotage and violence.

item.title: TIB urges accountability, political will to curb corruption
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman has said political commitment, accountability and independent institutions are essential to controlling corruption, calling on young people to play a stronger role in the anti-graft movement.
“Political will is the first condition for controlling corruption,” he said at the opening of TIB’s Inter-University Anti-Corruption Debate Competition 2026 at the CCDB Hope Centre in Savar on Friday.
He outlined four prerequisites for tackling corruption: political commitment, ensuring justice by holding those accused of corruption accountable, guaranteeing the effective independence of state institutions, and building public awareness and participation in the fight against graft.
Iftekharuzzaman said ordinary people bear the cost of corruption, often losing access to their legitimate rights and services despite having no involvement in corrupt practices.
“If we could control corruption even moderately, our GDP could grow by 2-3%. Effective control could prevent $16 billion from being siphoned out of the country annually,” he said.
He also stressed that disagreement should not turn people into adversaries, saying respect for differing opinions, tolerance and evidence-based arguments are values that should extend beyond debate competitions to national life.
The event brought together 32 university debate teams from across the country. Participants and judges took an anti-corruption oath administered by the TIB executive director.
TIB Outreach and Communication Director Mohammad Tauhidul Islam said the competition would help students exchange ideas and build connections, while encouraging them to become active participants in the anti-corruption movement.
The three-day residential competition, now in its fourth year, runs from November 26 to 28. The champion team will receive Tk50,000, the runner-up Tk30,000 and the best debater Tk10,000, along with crests and certificates.
At least one woman must be included in each debate team and judging panel. The top eight teams will also have the opportunity to participate directly in the next edition, subject to registration.

item.title: Dhaka airport’s third terminal set for breakthrough with Japan deal
item.description:
Ending months of uncertainty, the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) has finalised an agreement with a Japanese consortium to operate the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.
The agreement clears the way for the long-delayed terminal to become operational, with a formal signing ceremony scheduled for Monday and its inauguration planned for December 16.
After taking office, the government prioritised the terminal's launch and announced a roadmap to inaugurate it in December this year. However, its opening had remained uncertain amid prolonged negotiations between CAAB, the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, and the Japanese consortium.
CAAB Assistant Director (Public Relations) Kawsar Mahmud said a press briefing would be held at the authority's headquarters auditorium on Sunday.
At the briefing, CAAB Chairman Air Vice Marshal Md Mostafa Mahmud Siddiq will outline the details of the concession agreement for the third terminal, he said.
The agreement-signing ceremony will take place at 7pm on Monday at the InterContinental Dhaka, with Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat expected to attend.
The CAAB board approved the terms and conditions proposed by the Japanese consortium at its 321st meeting on November 10, following a review.
However, several of the consortium's proposed conditions had earlier triggered objections and controversy.
Among the most contentious were provisions to suspend international flight operations through the first and second terminals once the third terminal becomes operational and to prohibit the establishment of any other civil airport within a 100-kilometre radius for 15 years.
The conditions also drew criticism at a meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism.
Committee members questioned how the infrastructure and capacity of the first and second terminals, built with investments worth thousands of crores of taka, would be utilised if international operations were suspended there.
The possibility of operating separate terminals through multiple operators, as practised at several international airports, also came under discussion.
Concerns were raised that the proposed restrictions could limit the use of infrastructure developed through substantial public investment.
The agreement's financial terms also came under scrutiny.
Under the proposed revenue-sharing arrangement, Bangladesh was expected to receive 27% of the revenue. However, objections were raised over a provision offering the Japanese operator a special 13.5% discount during the transition from the Operational Partial Commercial Development (OPCD) phase to full Commercial Management and Development (CMD).
Separate fee and payment arrangements for Biman Bangladesh Airlines and ground-handling services were also discussed.
The third terminal was initially estimated to cost Tk13,610 crore. However, the project cost subsequently increased to around Tk22,000 crore following revisions and the inclusion of additional work.
Construction began on December 30, 2019. After more than 99% of the work had been completed, the terminal was soft-launched in October 2023.
Despite the soft launch more than two years ago, the facility remained non-operational as negotiations with the Japanese consortium had yet to be finalised.
Covering an area of 230,000 square metres, the third terminal is expected to significantly expand the airport's passenger-handling capacity.
The existing first and second terminals can accommodate around eight million passengers annually. With the addition of the third terminal, the airport's annual capacity is expected to rise to 20 million passengers.
The new facility will have parking space for 37 aircraft and feature 16 baggage conveyor belts, along with a range of modern passenger amenities and advanced technologies.
Several moving walkways will be installed to help passengers cover long distances inside the terminal more comfortably. Such facilities are widely used at major international airports, including those in Singapore and Bangkok.
The terminal will also feature three separate baggage-handling and storage facilities, modelled on those at Singapore's Changi Airport and Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport. These will include regular baggage storage, lost-and-found services and facilities for oversized luggage.
In addition to 16 regular baggage conveyor belts, four separate belts will handle oversized baggage.
Each washroom will have a dedicated baby-care lounge equipped with breastfeeding booths, diaper-changing stations and spacious family bathrooms.
A children's play area featuring slides and swings will also be available.
The terminal has already been equipped with health inspection rooms, first-aid facilities, testing centres for Covid-19 and other diseases, and isolation areas.
The terminal will have 10 self-check-in kiosks where passengers can enter their passport and ticket details to obtain boarding passes and seat assignments automatically.
Passengers can then drop off their luggage at designated points for automated transportation to the assigned aircraft.
However, baggage weighing more than the stipulated 30kg limit will not be accepted through this facility.
The terminal will also have 100 conventional check-in counters.
Movie lounges and airline lounges are expected to be introduced soon to provide passengers with additional facilities while waiting for their flights. Other installations have already been completed.

item.title: Bayern risk more than sporting success as Musiala saga rolls on
item.description:
Bayern Munich head to Hamburg on Saturday in the middle of a crisis which threatens not only to derail the club's sporting ambitions, but their identity itself.
Bayern, who are in the midst of an injury crisis which has decimated their forward line including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, sit two points behind Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga table.
But Bayern's treatment of midfielder Jamal Musiala by their hierarchy has led to a growing rift between the club and the playing group.
Shortly after Bayern lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday, ending their run as the final unbeaten team in Europe's top-five leagues this season, vice-captain Joshua Kimmich suggested the club had fallen out of step with their values.
"It's completely unacceptable and is not Bayern-like," Kimmich said on Wednesday, adding that Musiala's treatment was inconsistent with the club's "sense of togetherness".
This week, Bayern's hierarchy suggested Musiala take a pay cut as the 23-year-old battles his way back from a neurological condition which causes absence seizures.
While the condemnation from media, player unions and former players was swift, Kimmich -- who was wearing the captain's armband with Manuel Neuer out injured -- was the first member of Bayern's current squad to speak out.
Despite their status as one of football's perennial heavyweights, Bayern have always sought to emphasise their Bavarian roots and member-ownership in contrast to the American and Gulf-owned behemoths that loom over the European landscape.
But their cold-hearted treatment of Musiala, a fan-favourite and popular inside the dressing room, threatens their carefully crafted identity.
The club's vaunted 'Mia san mia' motto, which appears on every modern Bayern kit, translates to 'we are who we are'.
Midfielder Aleksandar Pavlovic, a product of Bayern's youth system, in 2025 said: "For me, 'Mia san mia' means being a family, standing together in good times and bad.
"That's what we live by here from a young age, that we always stick together."
Just two months after signing a contract extension in February 2025, Musiala began treatment for symptoms of the neurological condition.
After missing two months with an unrelated muscle injury, Musiala was warmly welcomed back by Bayern's 75,000-strong Allianz Arena on Friday.
Minutes after full-time, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested Musiala's condition meant he might be unable to deliver on his lucrative deal and should take a pay cut.
"If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation... because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," he said.
The firestorm began to spread immediately, with Bayern's untimely announcement of a record turnover of close to one billion euros ($1.1 billion) at their AGM a day later fanning the flames.
On Saturday, international player union FIFPRO said that Bayern "should know better", identifying a void between the German giants' values and their behaviour.
Former Bayern and Germany goalkeeper Oliver Kahn, who previously served as Bayern's CEO, issued a harsh critique.
"To put the player under pressure now and appeal to his decency through the public sphere, urging him to forgo part of his salary, is simply absurd," Kahn said.
But Kimmich's words have had the biggest impact as they provide a rare insight into the dressing room.
"It is understandable that the club might be concerned because of the illness. What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly," Kimmich said.
"It must not happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it."

item.title: New Zealand battle to 246-5 after day one of second India Test
item.description:
New Zealand fought to 246-5 at stumps Friday on the first day of the second Test against India, surviving a tricky day on a green seaming pitch.
Tom Blundell made a scrappy unbeaten 117-ball 53 in his 50th Test and Glenn Phillips was 36 from 64 balls at the end of the day in Christchurch.
Fast bowler Akash Deep was the best of India's bowlers taking 2-52 from 21 overs on a day their seam attack struggled to bowl threatening line or length.
Jasprit Bumrah was the only Indian bowler without a wicket.
There was plenty of help in a green pitch captain Shubman Gill chose to bowl on after winning the toss -- India's 10th toss win in 12 matches on their tour to New Zealand.
But his bowlers were guilty of not threatening the stumps enough throughout the day.
"Overall, it was quite good, but we could have done a bit better," Deep said of India's bowling performance.
"My self-realization was about how much I could force the batter to play.
"In my first spell of 5–6 overs, I tried to ensure the batter had to play 80 to 90 percent of the balls."
The Hagley Oval pitch had long and dense grass coverage, leading both captains to expect pace and bounce throughout the Test.
Blundell battled early, leaving well on length while holding his defensive shape so as not to nick several balls that went past his outside edge.
He picked his moments to counterpunch, cutting through the offside when offered width.
Blundell initially combined for a 74-run partnership with Daryl Mitchell, the two coming together with New Zealand in bother at 110-4 midway through the middle session.
Mitchell was out for 31, innocuously steering a Washington Sundar offspinner to Dhruv Jurel at leg slip.
Phillips then joined Blundell for a 62-run partnership in the last 20 overs.
Blundell was dropped on 49, edging to Yashasvi Jaiswal at gully, but he couldn't hold on to a difficult chance diving to his left.
"I think we did well to come back from where we were," Blundell said.
"The conditions are not easy out there. It's a wicket that I felt personally that you're never in.
"The ball's still doing quite a bit towards the end, so I think we'll take that today."
New Zealand captain Tom Latham made 59 earlier in the day, coming off two two-ball ducks in the drawn first Test in Wellington.
He made the most of a reprieve on 29 to make his 32nd Test 50.
He was removed caught behind from the bowling of Deep in the second session, a prodding defensive stroke only finding the edge as the ball nipped off the seam.
Henry Nicholls fell the next over, poorly pulling Anshul Kamboj to Deep on the fine leg boundary for 16.
Rachin Ravindra was also caught behind from Deep for 0, his third dismissal in three innings edging into the cordon.
Devon Conway was out for 31 with the last ball before lunch, lbw to debutant Gurnoor Brar.
India made one change to their starting side from the Wellington draw, offering a debut to speedster Brar in place of Prasidh Krishna.
New Zealand named an unchanged team.
New Zealand are third in the World Test Championship standings entering the match, while India sit fourth.

item.title: Tevez hopes Ronaldo will join Messi at testimonial
item.description:
Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them.
The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United.
Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires.
Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid.
If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side.
Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand.

item.title: India upbeat after 'very good' 2036 Olympics presentation
item.description:
Indian officials said they were confident of advancing to the next phase of the race to stage the 2036 Olympics after presenting plans for Ahmedabad as the host city.
The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) delivered an online presentation to the International Olympic Committee's Future Host Commission on Thursday, outlining its vision for staging the mega sporting event in the western city of Ahmedabad.
Ahmedabad, located in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's home state of Gujarat, is already set to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games in a key test of its organisational credentials.
"It was a very, very good presentation that was made," IOA chief executive Raghuram Iyer told reporters, saying discussions had been held at a "very macro level".
India is one of seven countries pursuing the 2036 Olympics, alongside Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Africa, South Korea and Turkey.
The Indian bid comes after internal disputes within the IOA.
Earlier this month the IOC warned the association to resolve governance issues, while president P.T. Usha announced she would not seek re-election in December after alleging a "big fraud" in the nomination process.
Iyer said the bid was in a "continuous dialogue" phase with the IOC, with successful candidates expected to move into a strategic dialogue stage next year.
"We are in this continuous dialogue phase and if you are successful you move onto the stage of strategic dialogue, which will happen in March or April."
He stressed that hosting an Olympics required backing from all levels of government.
"When a country is pitching for the Olympics, doing something so large it requires the complete support and backing of the city, of the state, of the union."
A final decision on the 2036 host is not expected until after the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, or in early 2029, he added.

item.title: 'Difficult' to topple Infantino, says Norway football boss
item.description:
The head of the Norwegian Football Federation Lise Klaveness, a fierce critic of FIFA president Gianni Infantino, acknowledged Thursday it would be "difficult" to topple him but the possibility was "still in play".
Klaveness has been critical of Infantino since 2022 when the World Cup was held in Qatar, and called for his resignation in August after several controversies during this year's World Cup hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.
"It will be difficult" to dethrone Infantino, Klaveness, a lawyer and former national squad player, told foreign media in Oslo on Thursday.
While European football confederation UEFA has rallied around French football chief Philippe Diallo's candidacy to take over the FIFA presidency in a March election, Infantino, who is running for re-election, still enjoys the support of the African, South American and Asian confederations, and is seen as the favourite.
"You cannot really know what's going to happen in such a volatile political world," Klaveness, 45, argued.
"So it might end up with a different candidate than Infantino for very many reasons."
"But as it seems now, he has a lot of support."
While the African (CAF) and South American (Conmebol) football confederations have reaffirmed their backing for Infantino, Klaveness pointed out that it is not they who vote, but the national federations, and that each vote is secret.
"That's why it's still in play," she said.
She also said she hoped that Diallo and the third candidate, Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japanese federation, would manage to join forces against Infantino.
At the head of FIFA since 2016, Infantino has been involved in several recent controversies, including accusations of running a one-man show, awarding a FIFA "peace prize" to Donald Trump, lifting the suspension of USA forward Folarin Balogun during the 2026 World Cup, and floating plans -- later abandoned -- to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights.

item.title: FIFA says hackers accessed limited personal, business information
item.description:
FIFA said on Thursday that it had been targeted in a cyberattack in which hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information”.
The world football governing body said it was working closely with relevant authorities, including law enforcement agencies, but did not disclose when the attack took place or the exact nature of the compromised information.
Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were FIFA files.
Three days later, the group appeared to claim responsibility for the breach in response to a post saying that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.
FIFA strongly condemned the unauthorised acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, saying such actions were a serious violation of privacy that could have significant consequences for those affected.
The cyberattack comes as FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino face scrutiny over a failed and secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino is also seeking to extend his 11-year presidency until 2031. He is considered the favourite in the election scheduled for March 18, with Japan's Kohzo Tashima and France's Philippe Diallo also in the race.
