Most garment workers return to work in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
The situation in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt has begun to return to normal after several days of labour unrest over demands for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Most garment workers returned to their jobs voluntarily on Thursday morning after accepting factory owners' offer of a minimum wage of Tk17,000, along with increased allowances.
Production has resumed at most factories, but workers at three factories are continuing their work stoppage. Meanwhile, 22 factories have declared general holidays, while another 21 remain closed under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act.
According to Industrial Police, the three factories where workers are continuing their work stoppage are Mango Tex, Green Life Knit Composite Ltd and Marma Composite. Some workers at these factories have stopped production, pressing for various demands, including a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, said workers began returning to factories and resuming their duties voluntarily on Thursday morning.
Production was continuing peacefully at most factories, and no untoward incidents had been reported in the industrial zone, he said.
He added that police remained on high alert, with additional personnel deployed in front of key factories to maintain stability.
For the past few days, Savar and Ashulia had witnessed work stoppages, protests and tension as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
In response, many factory owners offered a minimum wage of Tk17,000 and increased allowances. Many workers accepted the offer and returned to work, allowing production to resume at most factories.
However, workers at some factories are continuing to demand a Tk30,000 minimum wage, disrupting production at those establishments.
The 21 factories closed under Section 13(1) following management decisions have yet to reopen. Production at another 22 factories remains suspended due to general holidays.
Although the situation has improved across the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt, labour unrest persists at a number of factories.

item.title: Toufique remembered for fearless, independent journalism
item.description:
Friends, colleagues and prominent figures from different walks of life have remembered journalist and bdnews24.com founding editor Toufique Imrose Khalidi for his commitment to independent journalism, objectivity and forthrightness, saying his professional integrity remains an example for the country’s media.
They made the remarks at a memorial meeting titled “You Will Remain Silently in Our Hearts” at the Abdul Karim Sahitya Bisharad Auditorium of Bangla Academy in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon.
Water Resources Minister and MP Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, who said he had been close to Toufique since 1983, recalled their university days and described him as someone who offered candid advice on political matters without seeking an active role in politics.
Former Dhaka University Central Students’ Union general secretary Mostaq Hossain said Toufique raised sharp questions about political movements and taught him an essential principle of journalism: no one should be called a killer without evidence.
He also recalled Toufique’s efforts to establish bdnews24.com in 2006, when online journalism was still in its early stages in Bangladesh. Despite limited resources, Toufique believed in the venture and built it into a prominent news outlet.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah M Saleh said a journalist’s political beliefs should never obstruct the publication of the truth. He also called for reflection on the media’s past experiences and its role in fostering tolerance of differing views.
British citizen Julian Francis, who contributed to Bangladesh’s Liberation War, recalled how Toufique encouraged him to write about the 1971 genocide and speak openly about corruption and development. He said Toufique had assured him that bdnews24.com would stand by him if he faced trouble over his writing.
AB Party Chairman Mojibur Rahman Monju said political differences had not prevented him from recognising Toufique’s professional skills and distinctive thinking.
Biplobi Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque described him as principled and outspoken, saying his commitment to questioning those in power would inspire future generations.
Saiful Haque said one of the media’s key responsibilities is to question those in power and hold the government accountable. “Taufiq’s determination to uphold this responsibility of journalism would inspire future generations,” he said.
Among those attending the memorial were former BTV deputy director general KM Harun, Liberation War veteran Moniruzzaman Chowdhury, singer Sujit Mustafa, dancer Munmun Ahmed, physician Habibullah Talukder Raskin, fiction writer Mojaffor Hossain, former ambassador Ikhtiar Chowdhury, history researcher Hashem Sufi, Professor Mohammad Mohiuddin, journalist Mostafiz Shafi, senior lawyer Manzil Morshed, bKash CEO Kamal Quadir and Dhaka University Treasurer Professor Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, along with other distinguished guests from different professions.
Speakers said Toufique’s legacy would endure through the journalists he mentored and the example he set for independent, evidence-based reporting.
Former colleagues and current and former bdnews24.com staff also shared recorded tributes, recalling his leadership and contribution to journalism.

item.title: Two years since lawyer Alif's murder, father hopes to see justice
item.description:
Two years have passed since the murder of Saiful Islam Alif, a lawyer and assistant public prosecutor in Chittagong, but the trial has yet to reach a conclusion. His father says he hopes to live long enough to see justice delivered for his son.
Alif was hacked and beaten to death near the Chittagong court premises on November 26, 2024.
The court has accepted a charge sheet against 37 people, including Chinmoy Krishna Das, spokesperson for the Sanatani Jagaran Jote. Of the accused, 27 have been arrested and are in custody, while 10 remain at large.
Frustrated by the delay, Alif's family and colleagues have renewed their demand for justice. The Chittagong District Bar Association has announced a human chain and protest programme on the court premises. His family has also submitted a memorandum to the deputy commissioner, seeking the transfer of the case to a Speedy Trial Tribunal.
On November 26, 2024, Chinmoy Krishna Das, who had been arrested in Dhaka on sedition charges, was brought before a Chittagong court. After the court rejected his bail application, violence broke out in the court area.
According to the account provided, members of Iskcon attacked several structures, including the Courthill Jame Mosque. A confrontation then erupted between Iskcon members and local lawyers and litigants.
During the violence, Alif was hacked and beaten to death in front of Rangam Convention Hall. The attackers reportedly danced on his body after the killing.
Alif's father, Jamal Uddin, filed a case with Kotwali Police Station, naming 31 people as accused.
On July 1, 2025, the investigating officer, former assistant commissioner of the metropolitan police (Kotwali) Mahfuzur Rahman, submitted a charge sheet naming 37 people, with Chinmoy Krishna Das listed as the prime accused. The court accepted the charge sheet on August 25, 2025.
The other accused named in the charge sheet are Chandan Das Methor, Ripon Das, Rajib Bhattacharya, Shubho Kanti Das, Aman Das, Bunja, Ranab, Bidhan, Bikash, Ramit Prakash Das, Rumit Das, Nayan Das, Omkar Das, Bishal, Lala Das, Samir, Sohel Das, Shiv Kumar, Biglal, Parash, Ganesh, Om Das, Popy, Ajay, Debi Charan, Deb, Joy, Lala Methor, Durlabh Das, Sumit Das, Sonu Das, Saku Das, Bhajan, Ashik, Shahit, Shiba Das and Dwip Das.
Speaking to Bangla Tribune on Wednesday afternoon, Jamal Uddin said: “My son was murdered in broad daylight, in full public view. I will never get him back. I am getting old; I only hope to live long enough to see justice served for my son’s murder. I demand appropriate punishment for those who killed him.”
Assistant Public Prosecutor Md Raihanul Wazed Chowdhury, the lawyer for the case, said the court had accepted the charge sheet against 37 accused. Of them, 27 had been arrested, while 10 remained at large.
He said the charge sheet listed 49 witnesses, but only four had testified so far.
The plaintiff had submitted an application to the Chittagong deputy commissioner seeking the transfer of the case to a Speedy Trial Tribunal, but the request had not yet been granted, he added.
Aminur Rashid, assistant commissioner of police (Public Relations) at Chittagong Metropolitan Police, said efforts were under way to arrest the remaining accused.
“We are actively searching for the 10 accused who remain at large,” he said.

item.title: PM joins opening of National Livestock Week
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday joined the inaugural ceremony of the National Livestock Week-2026 as the chief guest.
The program is being held at the old Trade Fair Ground in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital, Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony said.
The Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock and the Department of Livestock Services jointly organised this year's event under the theme "Building the Nation through Export-oriented Livestock, Bangladesh First".
On the occasion, a three-day livestock fair and exhibition is being held at the venue, featuring 64 stalls and six pavilions.
The prime minister will distribute the National Livestock Awards among 23 recipients in eight categories in recognition of their contributions to the development and advancement of the livestock sector.
The National Livestock Week will be observed across all districts and upazilas of the country from Thursday until November 28 through various programs.

Fire at Lotto warehouse in Sherpur
item.description:
A fire at a warehouse of Italian footwear brand Lotto in Sherpur town on Wednesday gutted a large quantity of shoes and damaged an adjacent two-storey building.
The fire broke out around noon at the warehouse in the Khorompur area of the town.
Firefighters from Sherpur Fire Service rushed to the spot and brought the flames under control after nearly an hour of effort.
Although the quick response helped save nearby shops and houses from major damage, a large quantity of shoes stored in the warehouse was gutted, while the adjacent building suffered extensive damage.
Building owner Adil Mahmud Uzzal said he noticed earlier in the morning that someone had disconnected the electricity supply to his residence, suspecting foul play.
Uzzal Sheel, in-charge of Lotto's Sherpur outlet, said they had goods worth around Tk60 lakh in the showroom and warehouse combined.
He estimated the initial losses from the fire at around Tk25 lakh, adding that the actual amount could be determined after an audit.
Atiqur Rahman, deputy director of Sherpur Fire Service, said the cause of the fire would be known after an investigation.
Sherpur Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Khokon Chandra Ghosh visited the spot.

RMG entrepreneurs welcome new wage structure despite implementation challenges
item.description:
Garment industry entrepreneurs have welcomed the newly announced wage structure for readymade garment (RMG) workers, describing its implementation as challenging while pledging to enforce it from December 1.
Welcoming the government's initiative to form the Minimum Wage Board and announce the new wages within the shortest possible time, they said the revised structure would play an important role in meeting workers' expectations.
The entrepreneurs said although the wage hike would put some pressure on the industry considering its capacity, production costs and business realities, implementing the government-declared wages in compliance with the country's laws was their responsibility.
Executive President of the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) Fazle Shamim Ehsan told BSS that the newly announced wages were higher than the expectations of ordinary workers.
Although the decision would create some difficulties for factory owners, he welcomed it, saying entrepreneurs must comply with the wages fixed under the country's laws to continue doing business.
He expressed disappointment over the continuation of workers' movements even after the announcement of the minimum wages and hoped that workers would accept the government-declared pay structure and return to work soon.
He also said the owners would implement the new wages from December 1.
A K M Shaheed Reza , chairman of garment and textile manufacturing company Reza Group and former director of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), said wages for workers across different grades had increased by 36 to 43 percent under the new structure, making its implementation challenging for entrepreneurs.
However, he said they viewed the development positively.
He described the government's initiative to form the Minimum Wage Board and announce the new wages within a short time as commendable, adding that the process could have started earlier.
He said entrepreneurs appreciated the promptness and sincerity shown by the concerned authorities.
Shaheed Reza said today's entrepreneurs were keen to build a worker-friendly industry and, therefore, viewed the wage increase positively.
However, he noted that the new wage structure had brought the wages of Bangladeshi garment workers close to those in India and Pakistan, creating a new competitive challenge for the industry.
FBCCI Administrator Md Fazlul Haque said they welcomed the announcement of the minimum wages, which were higher than the expectations of many.
However, he said incidents of workers taking to the streets even after the wage announcement in some places needed to be examined carefully.
He said it is necessary to investigate whether any third party is instigating such developments, stressing that the situation should be handled with utmost caution.
He also pointed out that the financial condition of many factories is so difficult that even paying workers' salaries and allowances had become challenging.
Despite these constraints, he said entrepreneurs would implement the new wage structure from December 1.
The entrepreneurs stressed that maintaining a stable working environment alongside implementing the new wage structure was essential for the industry.
They said mutual cooperation and responsible conduct by workers and owners would help sustain production, employment and export growth in the sector.

item.title: 16 crude bombs recovered from CNG in Keraniganj; 2 AL activists held
item.description:
Police recovered 16 crude bombs from a CNG-run auto-rickshaw at a checkpoint in the Naya Bazar area of Keraniganj on Wednesday afternoon and arrested two Awami League activists, whose activities are banned, in this connection.
The arrestees were identified as Nazim and Akash, both reported to be local AL activists of the Dhaka-2 Constitutional area. Police arrested them on the spot for carrying the explosives.
Officer-in-Charge Ruhul Kuddus of Keraniganj Model Police Station said a police team intercepted a CNG auto-rickshaw at a regular checkpoint in Naya Bazar and seized 16 crude bombs (cocktails) from the vehicle.
Later, a bomb disposal unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) arrived at the scene and safely detonated the recovered crude bombs.
A case was filed under the Explosive Substances Act with Keraniganj Model Police Station on Wednesday evening, the OC added.

JU students block highway over fellow’s alleged assault by Army men
item.description:
Jahangirnagar University (JU) students blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway for around two and a half hours on Wednesday evening, protesting the alleged assault of a fellow student by some Army personnel.
The protesters took to the highway near the university's Dairy Gate around 7:30pm and blocked it, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks on both sides.
They placed four demands, including the dismissal and prosecution of the accused, a public apology from them in person, accountability for repeated incidents of this nature and payment of the victim's medical expenses.
The protesters, however, withdrew the blockade around 10:00pm after the senior Army officials talked to Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Nurul Islam and assured him they would look into the matter, said the VC.
The victim, Aurangzeb Ramjan, is a student of the Department of Economics from the 2023-24 academic session and a resident of Mir Mosharraf Hossain Hall.
Ramjan alleged that some Army men stopped the auto-rickshaw he was travelling in while on his way to provide tuition through Bismail in the afternoon and hit him with a stick.
Photo: UNB
“When I protested, the personnel took me to a nearby room and kicked and beat me,” he said.
JU Pro-VC (Academic) Prof Dr Md Shamsul Alam said the university administration was sympathetic to the students' protest and was working to resolve the issue.
Photo: UNB
Pro-VC (Administration) Prof Dr Mohammad Nazrul Islam said the VC had contacted the relevant higher authorities and a team was expected to visit the university to meet the victim and witnesses.

item.title: Illumina Innovation Day held in Dhaka
item.description:
Illumina, a global DNA sequencing leader, and its Bangladesh partner Invent Technologies Ltd organized “Illumina Innovation Day – Bangladesh 2026” at Renaissance Dhaka Gulshan Hotel on Tuesday, bringing together clinicians, scientists, and laboratory leaders to explore genomics applications in cancer care and infectious disease surveillance.
Participants included representatives from icddr,b, Child Health Research Foundation, Bangladesh Medical University, BIRDEM, Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission, and leading hospitals and diagnostic centres.
Illumina experts Fang Min Tan and Bi Chonglei showcased the MiSeq i100 benchtop sequencer, highlighting its applications in cancer research, genomic profiling, and data analysis, said a press release.
Invent Technologies General Manager (Life Science) Sheikh Md Selim Al Din discussed how genomic sequencing can help identify pathogens, monitor dengue, influenza, and tuberculosis outbreaks, and detect antimicrobial resistance within 24-48 hours.
Dr Mustak Ibn Ayub presented precision medicine in cancer management in Bangladesh and moderated a panel discussion on clinical genomics, testing costs, turnaround times, and developing local expertise.
Speakers stressed that expanding domestic genomic testing capacity could reduce costs and waiting times while strengthening cancer care and public health surveillance.
Invent Technologies also announced that its Central Dogma Lab in Mirpur, equipped with a MiSeq i100 Plus, is open for researchers and clinicians to test their own samples.

item.title: Awami League man dies while making crude bombs
item.description:
An activist of the activities-banned Awami League was killed and at least four others injured in an explosion while allegedly making crude bombs in Shibganj Upazila of Chapainawabganj on Wednesday afternoon.
The incident occurred around 2:30pm in the Chouka area of Monakasha Union, beside a field under a banana tree.
The deceased was identified as Md Thomas Uddin, 35, son of Md Mortuza of Lombartola village in Bishwanathpur. His Facebook profile identified him as a member of Shibganj Upazila Krishak League and an Awami League activist.
Shibganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Matiur Rahman said several people were making crude bombs at an isolated spot when one exploded, killing Thomas and injuring three to four others. The injured fled the scene afterwards.
Police recovered the body and sent it to the morgue of the 250-bed Chapainawabganj District Hospital for autopsy. An investigation is underway to determine the circumstances of the blast and identify those involved, the OC said.
Police Superintendent Gautam Kumar Biswas visited the scene later in the afternoon and said officers had recovered bomb-making materials along with the body.
Police had learned that the deceased was an activist of the activities-banned Awami League, although his organisational affiliation was still being verified, he said.
The SP said two or three other people might have been involved in making the explosives. Police suspect the materials were not being prepared for any legitimate purpose and are investigating the motive behind the activity.

item.title: Attorney general: Ziaul Ahsan’s role emerges in Narayanganj seven-murder case
item.description:
Former RAB officer Ziaul Ahsan’s alleged involvement in the 2014 Narayanganj seven-murder case has emerged in the confessional statements of convicted former RAB-11 commander Tarik Sayeed Mohammad, Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal has said.
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday after the first day of the Appellate Division’s hearing on appeals in the case, the attorney general said Tarik’s statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure described Ziaul’s instructions and role in RAB operations.
According to Kazal, Tarik said no operation could be conducted without Ziaul’s approval, who was then an additional director general (operations) at RAB headquarters.
The attorney general said case records and confessional statements described how five people were abducted first. Lawyer Chandan Sarker and his driver were later abducted after witnessing the incident.
All seven were killed after being rendered unconscious, and their bodies were dumped in a river with bricks and cement bags tied to them to prevent them from floating to the surface.
Kazal said the confessions detailed the planning, abduction and killings, and were consistent with other evidence in the case. However, Ziaul was not made an accused in the trial.
He said the state had argued before the Appellate Division in favour of upholding the High Court verdict, which sentenced 15 people to death, 11 to life imprisonment and nine others to different prison terms.
Additional Attorney General Barrister Anik R Haque said the prosecution had placed before the court extracts from the confessional statements of Tarik and four other accused, as there were no eyewitnesses to the killings.
The hearing is scheduled to continue on Thursday.

item.title: 10 development projects involving Tk24,110cr get ECNEC nod
item.description:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved 10 projects involving Tk24,110.66 crore.
Of the total, Tk 12,775.99 crore will come from the government's own funds, Tk 8,944.21 crore from project loans and Tk 2,390.47 crore from the agencies' own resources.
Prime Minister and ECNEC Chairperson Tarique Rahman presided over the meeting at the secretariat.
Of the 10 projects, five are new, four are revised and one has been granted a time extension.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare secured approval for two projects.
One is the second revision of the project to set up full-fledged cancer, heart and kidney treatment centres in eight divisional cities.
The other is the second revision of the project to build 500-bed medical college hospitals and ancillary buildings in Jessore, Cox's Bazar, Pabna and Noakhali, along with the vertical extension of the National Institute of Gastroliver Diseases and Hospital by adding 11th and 12th floors.
The Ministry of Social Welfare received approval for a fourth time extension of the project to set up a Bangladesh Poverty Alleviation Organisation health service centre in Charfesson Upazila.
Three projects of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives were approved.
These are the Pabna district rural infrastructure development project (PDRIDP), the rural infrastructure development project in Chittagong and Cox's Bazar districts, and the second revision of the important rural infrastructure development project in Noakhali, Feni and Lakshmipur districts.
The Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief got the nod for the proposed fourth revision of the second phase of the project to make rural earthen roads sustainable through herring bone bond (HBB).
Two projects of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources were also approved. One aims to enhance the capacity of electricity distribution systems of 13 Palli Bidyut Samitis near Dhaka under the Rural Electrification Board (REB), while the other will modernise and upgrade the REB's distribution system in Chittagong and Sylhet divisions.
The Ministry of Water Resources secured approval for a project to rehabilitate coastal polders 64/2A and 64/2B in Pekua Upazila of Cox's Bazar to improve flood control, drainage and irrigation.
The meeting was also informed about seven projects, each costing less than Tk50 crore, which the planning minister had already approved.
They are: Improvement of flood control, waterlogging removal and drainage in Chittagong City (second revision), Flood Reconstruction Emergency Assistance Project (FREAP), Conversion of plant quarantine laboratory at Central Packing House into an international-standard laboratory, Sustainable development and expansion of fisheries resources in Mymensingh division, Improvement of survey methods for fisheries resources of inland water bodies in Bangladesh, Strengthening of Venom Research Centre, Bangladesh (VRC,B) and Establishment of Textile Vocational Institute at Bhandaria in Pirojpur.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,363 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,363.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,258, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The two new suspected fatalities were reported across two divisions; Mymensingh and Khulna with one death each.
A total of 1,338 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 260,528.
During the same period, 74 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 26,374.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 233,259 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 224,287 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Bangladesh’s voter count rises to 12.92cr
item.description:
Bangladesh now has 12,92,29,749 registered voters, following an update to the electoral roll ahead of the upcoming local government elections, the Election Commission (EC) has announced.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed disclosed the figures at the Election Commission building in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
The updated list includes 452,106 new voters who turned 18 by October 31.
Of the total voters, 6,58,06,574 are men, 6,34,21,878 are women and 1,297 are from the third gender, Akhtar said.
The updated electoral roll will be used in the upcoming Union Parishad and other local government elections.

item.title: Govt plans Tk1,25,378cr Dhaka-Chittagong expressway
item.description:
The government has initiated plans to turn the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway into an access-controlled expressway.
The selected design includes 64km of elevated sections and 169km at ground level, stretching from Jatrabari in Dhaka to Sagarika intersection in Chittagong. Including 20 years of operational costs, the total expenditure is projected at Tk1,25,378 crore.
The Roads and Highways Department (RHD) is preparing to implement the project under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, potentially with foreign financing through a government-to-government arrangement. Work is targeted to begin in January 2027 and finish by December 2032, subject to approval.
The highway carries around 92% of the country's international trade and 81% of its export trade. Officials say the expressway aims to ease congestion, reduce transport costs and improve connectivity with industrial zones, export processing zones and the Chittagong Port.
The plan includes a 10-lane elevated section from Dhaka to Madanpur in Narayanganj, followed by a six-lane main highway with separate lanes for local traffic. It also proposes seven system interchanges, 29 service interchanges, 91 underpasses and dedicated truck parking at 15 locations.
BUET Civil Engineering Professor Dr Md Shamsul Haque said simply widening the highway would not resolve congestion, stressing the need for an access-controlled route with reliable speed and maintenance.
However, the project's financing structure and the proportion of elevated and ground-level sections remain under review. State Minister for Road Transport and Bridges Habibur Rashid said a final decision would follow an assessment of several proposals.
RHD Additional Chief Engineer Shishir Kanti Raut said a preliminary development project proposal had been submitted to the ministry, and construction would begin after approval.

item.title: Garment workers’ minimum wage rises 36% to Tk17,000
NBR cuts import duties on dates, apples, and oranges ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has reduced import duties on dates, apples, and oranges to keep their prices under control during the upcoming holy month of Ramadan.
According to a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, the import duty on dates has been slashed from 25% to 5%, bringing the total tax incidence on date imports down from 48% to 25%.
This reduced rate will remain in effect until March 10, 2027.
For apples and oranges, the regulatory duty has been reduced to 5%, while supplementary duty and VAT have been set at 20%.
Following these adjustments, the total tax incidence on apples and oranges will drop sharply from 121% to 48%.
The notification stated that the revised rates for apples and oranges will be effective from January 24 to February 23, 2027.
The NBR expects that the duty cuts will boost imports and ensure an adequate supply of these fruits, helping to stabilize market prices.
The decision to lower duties on these import-dependent fruits was reportedly taken a few days ago during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Currently, different varieties of dates are selling between Tk200 and Tk2,000 per kilogram in Dhaka’s kitchen markets, while apples are priced at Tk300–500 per kg and oranges at Tk400–600 per kg.

item.title: Mahila Parishad concerned over rising violence against women, children in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
Bangladesh Mahila Parishad’s Brahmanbaria district committee has expressed concern over a series of incidents of rape, sexual abuse, torture and murder involving women and children in the district.
The concern was raised at a press conference held at Brahmanbaria Press Club Wednesday afternoon, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women 2026.
Nelly Akter, vice-president of the district committee, chaired the event, while its general secretary, Shyama Sikder Dina, presented the written statement.
In her statement, Dina said poverty, social inequality and a lack of family and social awareness were among the factors contributing to violence against women and children.
She called for collective efforts to prevent such incidents, ensure justice and protection for survivors, and end the culture of impunity.
She identified Brahmanbaria Sadar, Akhaura and Nabinagar upazilas as areas with comparatively high numbers of reported incidents of violence against women and children.
Poverty, lack of family awareness, complexities within joint families, extramarital relationships and arrogance among some middle- and upper-income families were also cited as contributing factors.
According to the organisation, several incidents of violence against women and children were reported in the district between January and November 2026.
On April 11, a housewife was beaten to death in Nabinagar. On April 28, a teenage girl was reportedly raped in the Baganbari area of Ashuganj upazila.
On April 30, a doctor couple was arrested over allegations of torturing a 12-year-old domestic worker in North Mourail area of Brahmanbaria municipality.
In another incident, seven-year-old Mahida Akter was allegedly raped and strangled to death on September 25 in Andidil village under Talshahar Union of Ashuganj upazila.
A post-mortem report published on September 26 reportedly found evidence of rape and identified excessive bleeding and strangulation as the causes of death. The accused, Zahidul Islam, was arrested in connection with the case.
The organisation also cited the alleged rape of a five-year-old child with disabilities in Nasirnagar upazila and the rape of a madrasa student on October 7.
As part of the 16-day campaign marking the occasion, the district committee will conduct awareness programmes across the district from November 25 to December 10.
The programmes will include discussions with young people, women and men, meetings with administrative officials and lawyers, leaflet distribution, poster-drawing activities and other awareness initiatives.
Among those present were district committee vice-president Geeta Roy, publicity secretary Kohinoor Akter Priya, training secretary Masuma Khanam, movement secretary Ratna Das and committee member Laboni Rani Das.
Journalists from various print and electronic media outlets attended the press conference.

item.title: Batighar: A beacon of knowledge in remote villages of Tangail
item.description:
What began with around 100 books in a small room of his family home has grown into a community reading initiative with more than 2,000 books, 219 registered members and several thousand occasional readers.
Mohammad Kamruzzaman, a resident of Chourakorra village in Tangail's Magra Union, established the library, named Batighar, on February 21, 2010, while he was a university student.
Beyond its main library, the initiative has expanded to bus counters, railway stations and local salons, creating opportunities for people to read while waiting for buses, trains or haircuts.
Initially, Kamruzzaman used books from his personal collection and contributions from friends to set up the library in a room of his family home. Over the years, it has developed into a community resource where people of all ages can read books, borrow them and access information.
Readers can become members by following the library's rules. Books can be borrowed for 15 days, and those unable to visit the library can request delivery over the phone.
Kamruzzaman moved to Tangail town after completing his secondary education. He later enrolled at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University, where he studied in the Department of Criminology and Police Science. After graduation, he joined Bangladesh Police as a sub-inspector. He is currently serving at the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).
Seeking to make reading accessible beyond the library's premises, Kamruzzaman introduced mini libraries at different public places.
At Tangail's new bus terminal, several bus-counter mini libraries allow passengers to read while waiting for their buses.
He also launched a free reading programme at local salons, calling it the "Salon Mini Library". A total of 10 such libraries have been established at salons in Kuijbari, Ayanapur, Chourakorra, Nandabala and Magra Bazar in Tangail Sadar Upazila, as well as Palima Bazar in Kalihati Upazila.
A similar facility has been introduced at Tangail Railway Station, where a wooden bookshelf has been installed on the main platform. Passengers can choose books, read while waiting for their trains and return them afterwards.
Rakib Hossain, a passenger waiting for the Dhaka-bound Silk City Express, welcomed the initiative.
"This is a very commendable initiative. We often have to wait at the station for trains. The environment here is pleasant for reading. Now we can spend our waiting time reading books and enjoying ourselves," he said.
Several college students from the village help manage the library's activities.
Seema Akter, one of the student volunteers, said the library remains open from the afternoon until evening every day except Thursday.
"Books are regularly borrowed and returned during this time. Each book can be borrowed for 15 days. If someone has difficulty visiting the library, they can call us, and we arrange to deliver the book to them," she said.
Sumaiya Akter, a Class Ten student at Magra High School for Girls, said the library had made reading more accessible for students.
"Having this library has been very helpful for us. We can borrow books whenever we want," she said.
Local businessman Chhanowar Hossain, who enjoys reading during his leisure time, is also a regular member of the library.
Mahbub Hasan, a National University student and regular reader, said residents previously had to travel several kilometres to reach the district public library.
"Travelling there was difficult and time-consuming. Even when we wanted to read, we could not always manage to go. With this library, we now have much easier access to books," he said.
However, he said the collection and the library's furniture and other facilities needed further improvement.
Anisur Rahman, acting headteacher of Choudhury Malanch High School, said the library was helping develop reading habits among local residents.
"Alongside their textbooks, students are reading different kinds of books and enriching their knowledge. I believe this will help illuminate their future," he said, calling on education enthusiasts and financially capable members of society to support the library's development.
Kamruzzaman has received several awards for his contribution to promoting reading habits and establishing libraries in rural communities.
His recognitions include the Prothom Alo Bondhushava Award 2021, Pathshala Emerging Leader Award 2022, Institution Library Award 2023, Alor Ferry Library Digitisation Award and the Bangladesh Bookworm Association Special Recognition Award 2024.
Batighar's readers have also achieved recognition. Recently, library member Fawzia Haque Jinat was selected as the country's best participant at the school level in a national book-reading competition organised by the National Book Centre.
Kamruzzaman's father, Shahjahan, said he was initially doubtful about the initiative.
"When Kamruzzaman first established the library, I thought he was doing something unusual. But after a few days, I realised it was a very good initiative. That is why I allowed him to use a room in our house," he said.
Kamruzzaman said the initiative was intended to help people who love reading but cannot afford to buy books regularly.
To ensure the library's sustainability, he has formed a seven-member committee comprising local residents from different walks of life. The committee oversees its activities.
He is also trying to secure a permanent plot of land in the village to build a dedicated library.
"We are gradually moving forward with everyone's support. I hope that one day we will be able to establish our own building with a rich collection of books and publications from home and abroad," he said.
He added that the initiative also aims to encourage teenagers and young people to develop reading habits, reduce excessive dependence on technology and engage in social and humanitarian activities.
"We want to spread these activities across the district and, eventually, throughout the country," he said.
For Kamruzzaman, Batighar is more than a library. It is an effort to make books accessible to people who might otherwise have limited opportunities to read.

item.title: Dhaka urges South Africa to open resident mission
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Wednesday urged South Africa to consider opening a resident mission in Dhaka to strengthen political engagement, expand bilateral trade and streamline consular services.
He made the request when South Africa's non-resident High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Professor Anil Sooklal, paid a courtesy call on him at the foreign ministry here, according to a ministry press release.
Reaffirming Bangladesh's commitment to closer ties with South Africa, Kobir also called for simpler visa procedures for Bangladeshi businesspeople, officials, students and other travellers to the country.
Both sides noted the untapped potential for bilateral trade and investment.
Kobir called for establishing a Joint Trade Forum and exchanging high-level business delegations to boost trade.
The state minister thanked South Africa for its continued support for the Rohingya and urged it to remain engaged in international efforts to ensure their safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable return to Myanmar.

item.title: Christian Aid launches Asia model to strengthen local leadership
item.description:
International development and humanitarian organisation Christian Aid has launched a new Asia Multi-Country Cluster (MCC) model aimed at shifting more decision-making powers and resources to local organisations and communities affected by crises.
The model was launched at an event in Gulshan-2, Dhaka, on Tuesday. It seeks to promote locally led development by giving local partners greater control over development and humanitarian initiatives.
Christian Aid Chief Executive Officer Patrick Watt introduced the new operating structure, describing it as a shift away from traditional top-down management towards an approach that positions the organisation as a connector and convener of local partners.
State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam attended the event as chief guest, while NGO Affairs Bureau Director General (Secretary) Dr Mohammed Jakaria was present as special guest.
The event also highlighted Christian Aid's performance in the Grand Bargain Independent Report 2023–2026. According to the report, the organisation ranked first among global signatories in 2025, directing 82% of its humanitarian funding to local and national actors, against the Grand Bargain's target of 25%.
Christian Aid also outlined its Survivor and Community-Led Response (SCLR) approach, under which local self-help groups design and manage their own recovery projects rather than simply being consulted.
The organisation also highlighted its efforts to promote fair indirect cost recovery (ICR) for local partners, speed up emergency fund disbursement during disasters and simplify due diligence procedures.
Representatives of Bangladeshi partner organisations, including Bazle Mustafa Razee of FIVDB, Juliate Keya Malakar of CCDB and Sunzida Sultana of Karmojibi Nari, shared their experiences of working with Christian Aid.
Senior members of the Asia MCC team, including Head of Impact Douwe Dijkstra, Partnership and Strategy Lead Nuzhat Jabin, Operations Lead Azahar Ali and Bangladesh Programme and Partnership Lead Prince Baroi, discussed how the new structure would promote regional collaboration, cross-country learning and local leadership.

item.title: Bellingham beauty in Real win as Arsenal, City held in Champions League
item.description:
Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season's Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home.
Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels.
Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season's league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points.
Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart.
Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net.
Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club.
Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho's side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions.
"That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment," England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal.
Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively.
- Como and Betis flying -
Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia.
Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game.
Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard's cross late on.
It is the second time Arsenal, last season's beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.
Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca's side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli.
Rasmus Hojlund, formerly of Manchester United, gave the Italians the lead early in the second half only for Ayyoub Bouaddi to equalise.
Kevin De Bruyne was returning to face his former side and he saw his Napoli team retake the lead through Noa Lang in the 76th minute, but Rayan Cherki's fine late goal earned City a point.
City won 10 of their first 11 games this season under Maresca. But the wheels have come off in the wake of the club being found guilty of widespread breaches of Premier League financial rules.
- Aston Villa lose -
"We don't like these moments - we want to win games - but unfortunately this moment is like this," said Maresca, ahead of a trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.
None of the Premier League's representatives in the competition won on Tuesday, with Villa losing 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul as Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game late on. The two clubs are now level on nine points in the standings.
Portuguese champions Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord thanks to Oussama Targhalline's early own-goal, while Antonio Nusa netted twice as RB Leipzig beat Lens 3-1 -- that was a fourth straight Champions League loss for the French team.
A stoppage-time own-goal gave Bodo/Glimt a 1-0 victory against Austria's LASK in Norway.

item.title: Saudi coalition says struck Yemen port city, Houthis threaten retaliation
item.description:
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said Wednesday it had struck Yemen’s key port city of Hodeida, while the Iran-backed group threatened to retaliate as the conflict further escalated.
The Houthis also claimed responsibility for attacks a day earlier on the Saudi capital that struck the tallest tower in its financial district, wounding 11.
In recent weeks the group has launched a barrage at Saudi targets including the financial district, airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
The Saudi coalition has been striking Houthi-held areas of Yemen in support of the internationally recognized government, which has been battling the Houthis for territory since a civil war reignited in July.
“We targeted operational capabilities at the port of Hodeida,” the coalition posted to X on Wednesday, having earlier warned civilians to evacuate.
Hodeidah is under Houthi control and is a key entry point for goods into Yemeni territory held by the group.
Houthi media outlet Almasirah confirmed Hodeida had been targeted but did not provide details. No casualties or injuries were reported.
Almasirah added that Saudi forces had also attacked the area’s international airport.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree early on Wednesday threatened to retaliate against Red Sea ports in Saudi Arabia if the coalition went ahead with strikes on Hodeida.
“The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats,” he posted on Telegram.
Saree warned civilians near Saudi ports to “evacuate immediately” and called for “all shipping companies to remove their vessels from these ports at once.”
Months into the renewed war, Saudi Arabia appears increasingly unable to shield even its most sensitive infrastructure from attacks, with the Houthis striking strategic facilities across the kingdom and prominent skyscrapers in the heart of Riyadh.
On the ground in Yemen, the Houthis are pressing their advance against government forces, forcing them to retreat. Houthi fighters are positioned just 60 kilometers (37 miles) from Aden, the government’s main stronghold in the south.
A Yemeni military spokesman said this week that they were preparing Aden’s defenses for a potential attack.
In a sign of mounting pressure on Riyadh, Saudi Arabia last week removed its top general overseeing its military campaign, in what appeared to be an effort to inject new momentum into the war and contain their adversaries.
On Tuesday, the Saudi capital’s tallest skyscraper was struck for a second time in days, wounding 11 people.
The Houthis claimed responsibility on Wednesday, also saying they struck the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom’s oil-rich east.
Saree described the refinery attack as “accurate and direct”, saying it “caused fires to break out at the facility.”
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said early Wednesday they had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura, resulting in falling shrapnel but no reported injuries.
Saree said the Houthi attack on Riyadh was carried out in three phases, with strikes also hitting their targets “accurately.”
The Riyadh attack struck the PIF tower, which houses the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. The building had already been targeted last Thursday and is one of several high-profile sites hit since fighting resumed in the summer.
Attacks on the PIF are symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy -- a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.
Qatar and Pakistan, who have been acting as mediators in efforts to end the wider regional war between Iran and the United States, both “strongly” condemned the attack on the building.
Two Indian citizens were wounded in the attack, Delhi’s foreign ministry said.

Police disperse garment workers attempting to block road in Savar
item.description:
Garment workers in Hemayetpur, Savar, tried to block a road on Wednesday while demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, leading to a clash with police. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters and restore order.
The incident occurred around 8:45am near Bagbari intersection in Hemayetpur.
According to witnesses and police sources, workers initially arrived at their respective factories on time. However, shortly afterwards, workers from several factories stopped working and walked out, gathering on the Hemayetpur-Singair road in an attempt to block it.
The protesters also visited nearby factories that were still operating and urged workers there to stop production and join the demonstration. There were reports that some factories were targeted with bricks and stones thrown from outside, in apparent attempts to vandalise the premises.
The workers eventually gathered at Bagbari intersection and began protesting, disrupting traffic on the road.
Industrial Police and local police arrived after receiving reports of the blockade. When the workers refused to clear the road, police fired tear gas shells to disperse them.
Additional police and law enforcement personnel have been deployed at key locations across the industrial zone, including Bagbari intersection and Hemayetpur. Patrols have also been intensified to prevent further unrest.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Industrial Police-1, said production had been suspended at 41 factories across the Savar and Ashulia industrial zones amid the ongoing movement for a higher minimum wage.
Of these, authorities at 22 factories have declared indefinite closures under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, under the “no work, no pay” provision. Workers at 10 factories have stopped work over wage demands, while nine factories have declared general holidays for Wednesday to prevent untoward incidents amid the unrest.
Law enforcement personnel remain on high alert to maintain order across the industrial areas as workers continue their protests.

item.title: Auto-rickshaw driver killed, 3 injured in bus collision in Jatrabari
item.description:
An auto-rickshaw driver was killed and 3 others, including 2 Qatar-bound passengers, were injured after a bus hit their vehicle in Raerbagh, Jatrabari, Dhaka, on Wednesday morning.
The deceased was identified as Masum Mia, 40. The injured were identified as Md Bashir, 33, and Qatar-bound passengers Kawsar Hossain Rubel, 31, and Al Amin, 30.
The injured were taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where doctors declared Masum dead. The 3 injured are receiving treatment.
Bashir's wife said Rubel and Al Amin were scheduled to fly to Qatar at 11:30am on Wednesday. They were travelling by auto-rickshaw from in front of Baganbari Mosque in Raerbagh, Shonir Akhra, towards the main road, where they planned to take a CNG-run auto-rickshaw to the airport.
Her husband was accompanying them, she added.
When the auto-rickshaw reached Raerbagh bus stand, a bus hit it and drove away, causing the vehicle to overturn and injuring all 4 occupants, she said.
Locals rescued the injured, and their families took them to the hospital after being informed of the accident.
Rubel and Al Amin are from Ramganj upazila of Lakshmipur.
Masum was the son of Harun Hawlader of Mondopasha village in Uzirpur upazila of Barishal.
Sub-Inspector Md Selim of the DMCH police outpost confirmed the incident, saying Masum's body had been kept in the hospital morgue and the injured were receiving treatment in the emergency department.

item.title: Police killings, station arson fuel public anxiety
Inmate surge pushes prisons beyond capacity, putting rights at risk
item.description:
Bangladesh’s prisons are grappling with severe overcrowding, with nearly 117,000 inmates being held in facilities designed to accommodate just over 45,000, putting enormous pressure on accommodation, sanitation, healthcare and daily operations.
The scale of the crisis means that, on average, 259 inmates are sharing space intended for every 100. The overcrowding is depriving many prisoners of adequate rest and exposing them to serious health risks.
The situation is particularly alarming for sick inmates, as prison authorities struggle to provide adequate medical care. An increase in arrests in political cases and the prolonged detention of accused persons awaiting trial have further aggravated the problem.
Overcrowding in the country's 68 prisons has thus become more than an administrative challenge, raising serious concerns over human rights and public health.
According to the Department of Prisons, the country's 68 prisons had a combined capacity of 45,186 inmates as of November 22. However, they were holding 116,956 prisoners as of November 23, exceeding their capacity by 71,770.
Of the total inmates, 4,020 are women, while 2,483 are on death row and 170 enjoy division status, according to prison authorities.
Sources said a recent rise in arrests in political cases had added to the pressure on an already overstretched prison system. With a significant number of those arrested being sent to prison, facilities operating beyond capacity are facing further strain.
The impact is being felt across accommodation, food, healthcare, security and overall prison management.
According to prison authorities, the capacity of a prison is determined by the number of inmates it can accommodate while ensuring adequate sanitation, healthcare and security. When the population exceeds twice that capacity, however, every aspect of prison management comes under additional pressure.
A shortage of living space, inadequate ventilation and unhygienic conditions can adversely affect inmates' physical and mental health.
Healthcare is among the most pressing concerns. Although the country's prisons are designed to accommodate just over 45,000 people, more than 116,000 are currently being held there. Providing medical services to such a large population has become increasingly difficult with limited manpower and existing facilities, prison sources said.
Experts warn that overcrowding increases the risk of infectious diseases spreading among inmates. It also makes regular monitoring and treatment difficult for prisoners suffering from chronic conditions such as heart disease, kidney disease, diabetes and hypertension.
Inadequate rest and poor living conditions can further aggravate the health risks for these inmates.
Medical emergencies at night pose an additional challenge. Conditions such as heart attacks, strokes and acute breathing difficulties require immediate medical attention. But overcrowding, limited healthcare facilities and delays in transferring inmates to hospitals can increase the risk of fatal outcomes.
Those concerned say any possible role of delayed treatment or negligence in deaths inside prisons should be thoroughly investigated.
Human rights activists say prison overcrowding cannot be treated simply as a shortage of space. It directly concerns inmates' fundamental rights, human dignity and the state's responsibility to protect them.
Even those detained on criminal charges or convicted of offences retain the right to necessary medical care, safe accommodation and humane living conditions.
Human rights activist Abu Ahmed Faizul Kabir told Dhaka Tribune that overcrowding was undermining inmates' rights to adequate personal space, proper lighting and ventilation, hygienic conditions, rest and medical care.
"Living in cramped conditions increases the risk of infectious diseases and adversely affects inmates' physical and mental health," he said.
"We must remember that imprisonment means restricting a person's freedom, not stripping them of their human dignity and fundamental rights. The prolonged detention of accused persons awaiting trial and delays in the judicial process are making the situation even more complicated," he added.
Faizul Kabir said building new prisons or expanding the capacity of existing facilities alone would not resolve the crisis. Reducing delays in the judicial process, ensuring bail in bailable cases and introducing effective alternatives to unnecessary imprisonment were equally important.
"Alongside expanding prison capacity and improving facilities, it is essential to ensure bail in bailable cases, expedite trials and strengthen alternatives to unnecessary incarceration. The state must take initiatives to transform prisons into centres of reform and rehabilitation, rather than places of punishment alone," he said.
The growing inmate population has also become a major challenge for prison administration. Authorities are struggling to meet the daily needs of a large number of prisoners with limited infrastructure, manpower and medical facilities.
Maintaining discipline while ensuring inmates' security, healthcare and other essential services has placed additional pressure on the administration.
Inspector General of Prisons Brig Gen Md Anwarul Kabir told Dhaka Tribune that overcrowding was a reality the authorities had to manage.
"This is the reality, and we have to accept it. We are trying to manage the situation temporarily with the support and resources available to us," he said.
Asked about inmate deaths and accountability in such cases, he said the authorities immediately investigated the circumstances surrounding each death to determine whether negligence was involved.
"Whenever an inmate dies, we immediately look into the cause of death and whether there was any negligence or anyone was responsible. If anyone is found responsible, departmental action is taken against them," he said.
Those concerned warn that the situation could deteriorate further unless prison infrastructure, healthcare facilities and manpower are expanded in line with the growing inmate population.
They stress that addressing the crisis requires both judicial and administrative measures to reduce the number of prisoners and sustained investment in improving prison accommodation and healthcare services.

item.title: RMG wage talks: Workers cut demand to Tk22,000, owners raise offer to Tk15,700
Child marriage rates return to 2006 levels among adolescent girls
item.description:
Child marriage among adolescent girls in Bangladesh has surged since 2019, wiping out 13 years of progress and pushing the prevalence of marriage among girls aged 15–19 back to levels last recorded in 2006, according to data presented by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).
The Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) 2025 shows that 38.9% of girls aged 15–19 are currently married, up from 32.9% in 2019. The increase of 6 percentage points has reversed the progress recorded over the preceding 13 years, when the rate stood at 39% in 2006.
The findings were presented at a dialogue organised by UNFPA in Dhaka on Tuesday, bringing together senior editors and journalists from newspapers, television channels, online news portals and news agencies to discuss proposed reforms to the Child Marriage Restraint Act (CMRA) 2017 and the media's role in addressing child marriage.
Presenting the findings, Iliza Azy, chief of the Adolescents and Youth Unit at UNFPA Bangladesh, highlighted the reversal in progress, drawing on data from MICS, the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) and UNICEF covering 2006–2025.
The data also shows that the proportion of girls aged 15–19 married before 18 increased from 28% in 2019 to 33.9% in 2025. Meanwhile, the proportion married before reaching 15 rose from 7.6% to 9.7% over the same period.
The increase has been widespread, with 51 of the country's 64 districts recording a rise in adolescent marriage rates, 19 of which were statistically significant.
Chandpur recorded the steepest increase in marriages before 18, at 19.8 percentage points, followed by Khulna at 18.9 percentage points.
In 2025, Chapainawabganj had the highest prevalence of girls aged 15–19 married before 18, at 53.5%, followed by Satkhira at 51.3%.
Despite the recent reversal among adolescents, the longer-term figures for women aged 20–24 show some progress. According to MICS 2025, 47.2% of women in this age group were married before 18, down from 64.1% in 2006 and 51.4% in 2019.
However, the survey highlights significant socioeconomic and regional disparities. Child marriage before 18 was recorded among 62.5% of women from the poorest households, compared with 31.5% among those from the wealthiest households.
The prevalence was also higher in rural areas, at 49.4%, than in urban areas, at 42.5%.
A joint UNFPA-UNICEF legal review of the CMRA 2017 and its 2018 Rules identified several gaps that limit legal protection for girls. Although the law criminalises child marriage, it does not automatically invalidate the marriage itself.
The review particularly flagged Section 19, which allows marriage below the legal age under special circumstances with a court order, without specifying a minimum age or providing adequate safeguards. It also identified weaknesses in birth and marriage registration, forged birth certificates, inactive child marriage prevention committees and limited prosecutions.
The joint recommendations include repealing Section 19, setting a uniform minimum marriage age of 18 for both women and men, making child marriages voidable at the request of the child, removing criminal liability for children and extending the complaint-filing period from two to six years.
UNFPA Representative in Bangladesh Catherine Breen Kamkong said a law against child marriage could protect girls only when they were aware of their rights and could access an accountable justice system.
She stressed the importance of accurate media reporting on the law and the lived experiences of girls married as children to help policymakers understand the need for reform and raise public awareness about keeping girls in education.
At the dialogue, media professionals committed to expanding evidence-based and ethical reporting on child marriage and contributing to national efforts to reduce the practice.
The event was organised in partnership with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, ahead of the inaugural International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage on November 27.

item.title: Govt employees face double rent for retaining quarters after transfer
item.description:
Government employees who continue occupying official residences after being transferred outside Dhaka and Chittagong city corporation areas will have to pay double the prescribed rent, the Directorate of Government Accommodation has warned.
In a notice, the directorate asked officials and employees to vacate government quarters within the stipulated period under the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982.
The notice said government employees working in the two city corporation areas are eligible for accommodation allocated by the directorate. However, many fail to inform the directorate after being transferred elsewhere for official reasons, while some continue occupying their quarters beyond the permitted period.
Such practices violate the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982, it said.
Employees authorised to retain government accommodation after being transferred outside the designated areas will be charged double the applicable house rent allowance after the stipulated period, according to the notice.
The directorate said many employees claim they are unaware of the double-rent provision and seek waivers on the grounds that their continued occupancy was authorised. However, it has no authority to waive the additional rent payable to the government under the rules. Similar instructions had been issued previously, it added.
Under Rule 15(2) of the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982, employees allotted government accommodation must vacate it within two months of dismissal, removal from service, expiry of a contractual appointment, resignation, transfer, deputation abroad or retirement.
Rule 15(3) allows the government to extend an employee's occupancy for up to six months in cases of dismissal, removal, resignation, retirement or transfer if retaining the accommodation is essential for their children's education.
Meanwhile, Rule 19(1) stipulates that employees authorised to retain government accommodation must pay rent at twice the rate of their entitled house rent allowance under the national pay scale.
The directorate has urged the concerned authorities to ensure strict compliance with the rules, take necessary action within the stipulated timeframe and inform their subordinate officials and employees accordingly.

item.title: 2 die after inhaling toxic gas in Satkhira septic tank
item.description:
Two people died, and two others fell sick after inhaling toxic gas from a septic tank in Kaliganj upazila of Satkhira district on Tuesday.
The deceased were identified as Mahananda Sarkar, 35, son of Sanatan Sarkar, and Md Arafat, 16, son of Moni Par, of Bareya village.
Local people said Mahananda went to the septic tank of one Ashraf to clean it and died on the spot after inhaling toxic gas.
Later, Arafat also went to see Mahananda’s condition and died there.
Meanwhile, Golam Hossain, joint convener of Tarali union unit of Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal and another person also fell sick as they went to the septic tank while trying to rescue those trapped inside.
However, local people rescued Golam Hossain and the other person and took them to Satkhira Medical College Hospital, said Enamul Haque, a member of Tarali Union Parishad.

item.title: Supply of winter vegetables, high egg production drive down egg price
item.description:
Prices of eggs have decreased by Tk20-25 per dozen over a month. In Rangpur, farmers were selling brown eggs at between Tk9.40 and Tk10.25 per egg on 6 November, compared to Tk11 a month earlier. The retail price of the same eggs in Dhaka fell to Tk10.8 per egg, down from Tk13.3 per egg a month earlier. Farmers estimate their production cost per egg at about Tk9.5.
Stakeholders say that the supply of winter vegetables usually triggers a fall in demand for eggs. They say that consumers complain about an egg syndicate when egg prices are high. However, when prices are low, it becomes obvious that there is no syndicate.
Aminur Rahman (48), owner of 7,000 layer hens in three sheds in Hasnabad of Rangpur Sadar, left his father’s tobacco business and started with 2,000 birds four years ago. He is currently producing at 92% (92 eggs per 100 hens each day) but he is concerned about falling egg prices with the arrival of early varieties of winter vegetables. "An increased supply of vegetables has pushed down egg prices, from Tk11.80 per egg earlier to Tk9 per egg. Supply of cheap vegetables reduces demand for eggs. I fear that the price will fall further during the peak season of winter vegetables," he told this author.
A Bachelors student of agriculture science, Rokonuzzaman Mugdho (23), son of Mohammad Mukul of Thakuradaho of Gangachara, has assumed responsibility of running a farm with 9,000 hens. His father began with 1,000 layer birds in 2014. "I am surprised that the price has fallen so early. Chickens lay more eggs during the winter, and availability of vegetables normally causes the egg price to fall. The market rate of our eggs has declined by almost Tk2 per piece, and the peak season of vegetables is yet to arrive," he said. His father added: "I don't worry too much about the market, I focus on my own farming and business. Layer is a long-term investment and in the short term it can be frustrating. No one can control the price, other than the market itself."
Khandakar Abu Sayeed, a school teacher and poultry farmer in Poran area of Pirgachha, started layer farming with 1,000 birds in 2011. Some 17,000 of his 20,000 hens are laying eggs now. He mentioned that lower production of vegetables and fish pushes up the demand for eggs during the summer when egg supply is usually low. "In winter, vegetables are abundant, commercial egg production increases by at least 5 per cent, and production of duck eggs by 20% or so," he said, explaining the fall in egg prices.
Abdus Salam (35), a trader at Taraganj Bazar, Rangpur, used to sell 7 or 8 thousand eggs at Tk11 each day only a month ago. Despite the price fall by Tk1.5 per egg in his area, he can’t sell more than 5,000 eggs each day now. "Earnings of working people and low income people have fallen, and during winter they buy vegetables, that's why demand for eggs fell," he argued.
In the business hub of Saidpur in northern district of Nilphamari, Shafiqul Islam (54), owner of a wholesale store, said that the price of eggs fluctuates with demand and supply. "Higher supply of eggs and availability of vegetables prompted a price decline." He added that "some people blame producers and traders for price volatility, without truly understanding the market."
Kazi Zahin Hasan, director at Kazi Farms, observed that vegetables and eggs are substitutes for each other. "When winter vegetables become available, consumers prefer to buy winter vegetables, and buy fewer eggs. So the demand for eggs falls in winter, and the price of eggs also falls," he said. “Earlier this year, in summer, we saw that excessive rain flooded vegetable fields, and reduced the supply of vegetables. That prompted consumers to buy more eggs. The demand for eggs increased, and the price also increased. Many government officers expect the price of eggs to be stable, but this expectation is not realistic. When supply exceeds demand, the price will be low. When demand exceeds supply, the price will be high."

item.title: Nine more children die with measles symptoms
item.description:
Nine more children died with measles symptoms in the 24 hours until 8am on Tuesday, while 1,351 suspected and confirmed cases were reported across the country, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said.
With the latest fatalities, the number of deaths from suspected measles has risen to 1,256 since March 15. No deaths from confirmed measles were reported during the latest 24-hour period, keeping the confirmed death toll at 105.
The combined death toll from confirmed measles and measles-like symptoms has now reached 1,361 since March 15.
The DGHS said 1,283 suspected cases and 68 confirmed cases were reported in the 24 hours until 8am Tuesday.
Since March 15, the country has recorded 259,190 suspected cases and 26,300 confirmed cases, according to the latest DGHS data.
A total of 231,999 patients with suspected measles have been admitted to hospitals nationwide since March 15. Of them, 223,158 have been discharged, the release added.

item.title: Govt plans 3,000 electric buses to overhaul Dhaka’s public transport
item.description:
The government plans to introduce 3,000 modern, environment-friendly electric buses in phases to bring discipline to Dhaka’s chaotic public transport system, improve passenger services and reduce air pollution.
The initiative will initially be launched under government management through the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC), with plans to gradually bring private bus operators under the new system.
The plan was announced at a meeting on public transport reform and implementation of the "gross-cost" model under the World Bank-funded Bangladesh Clean Air Project (BCAP) at the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry on Tuesday.
Road Transport, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam chaired the meeting.
The minister said the government aims to make Dhaka’s public transport system modern, safe, affordable and passenger-friendly through the phased introduction of 3,000 electric buses.
He said merely increasing the number of buses would not resolve the problems, stressing the need for structural changes to the existing operational system.
The transformation could take two to three years, with World Bank support.
Under the proposed gross-cost model, buses will operate through tripartite agreements involving the Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA), bus operators and vehicle suppliers, replacing the conventional route-permit-based system.
Fares collected from passengers will be deposited with the authorities, which will pay operators at a fixed rate per kilometre based on compliance with prescribed service standards, rather than passenger numbers or fare collections.
The model is expected to reduce unhealthy competition among buses for passengers, ensure adherence to schedules and improve transparency and accountability in operations.
The introduction of electric buses is also expected to reduce vehicle emissions and improve air quality.
However, the initiative will require charging infrastructure, maintenance facilities, skilled manpower, route restructuring and effective monitoring.
State Minister for Road Transport and Railways Habibur Rashid, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammed Ziaul Haque, World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan Jean Pesme, representatives of the World Bank and senior officials concerned attended the meeting.

item.title: SRB: No cause for public alarm over December rumours
item.description:
There is no reason for the public to be alarmed about November, December or January despite various claims circulating on social media about December, said Lieutenant Colonel Md Hafizur Rahman, commanding officer of Special Response Battalion (SRB)-4.
He made the remarks in response to questions from journalists at a press conference at the SRB Media Centre in the capital's Karwan Bazar on Tuesday.
He said people had encountered similar warnings in the past and urged the public not to be anxious.
The SRB official said workers' recent demands for higher wages were legitimate, but some saboteurs had used the protests as a cover to carry out acts of vandalism.
He added that various statements and warnings about December had been circulating on social media.
According to Hafizur, a significant number of people allegedly involved in sabotage, including crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson, had been arrested.
He thanked members of the public for helping prevent such incidents, saying many suspected saboteurs had been apprehended by local residents and handed over to police.
“We are doing our utmost. I would like to extend a special thanks to the local residents, as many of these saboteurs were apprehended by the courageous public and handed over to the police,” he said.

item.title: 174 undocumented Bangladeshis return from Libya
item.description:
A total of 174 undocumented Bangladeshis who were stranded in Libya and wished to return home voluntarily have been repatriated.
They arrived in Dhaka at 4:45am on Tuesday aboard Buraq Air flight UZ-222.
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the repatriation was carried out with the joint cooperation of the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, the Libyan government and the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
Most of the returnees had entered Libya illegally after being lured and assisted by human traffickers, hoping to reach Europe by sea, the ministry said. Many reportedly faced abduction and torture in Libya.
Officials from the foreign ministry, other relevant ministries and IOM welcomed them at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.
The foreign ministry urged the returnees to share their harrowing experiences to raise public awareness about the risks of irregular migration.
IOM provided each returnee with travel expenses, food supplies and basic medical care, as well as temporary accommodation where necessary.
The ministry also said it was working with the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and IOM to safely repatriate other Bangladeshis held at detention centres across Libya.
